What is doxx?
- doxx is a terminal-native viewer for Word files — it “expose[s] the contents of .docx files without leaving your terminal.”  
- It renders formatting, tables, equations and images without Microsoft Word.

Key viewing features
- Rich terminal rendering: preserves bold/italic/headers, lists, and smart tables with alignment.
- Equation support: LaTeX rendering for inline and display equations.
- Images: inline terminal images (Kitty, iTerm2, WezTerm, Sixel or fallbacks).
- Fast search with highlighting and interactive outline/navigation.
- Copy-to-clipboard and copy-search-with-context features.
- Configurable keymaps (default, vim, less) and custom bindings.

Export formats
- Exports: markdown, text, csv, json, ansi.
- Note: CSV export extracts only tables (tables-only extraction for data workflows).

Installation (summary of commands)
- Homebrew (macOS/Linux): brew install bgreenwell/tap/doxx
- Cargo (cross-platform): cargo install doxx
- Debian/Ubuntu: sudo apt install doxx (packaged as rust-doxx)
- Arch / AUR: pacman -S doxx ; yay -S doxx-git (dev)
- Nix: nix profile install github:bgreenwell/doxx
- Conda-Forge: conda install doxx  (or via pixi global install doxx)
- NetBSD: pkgin install doxx
- Pre-built binaries (macOS/Linux auto-detect): curl -L https://github.com/bgreenwell/doxx/releases/latest/download/doxx-$(uname -s)-$(uname -m).tar.gz | tar xz && sudo mv doxx /usr/local/bin/
- Build from source: git clone https://github.com/bgreenwell/doxx.git && cargo install --path .  (or cargo build --release)

Supported platforms
- Linux (statically linked x86_64-unknown-linux-musl)
- macOS (x86_64 and aarch64 Apple Silicon)
- Windows (x86_64-pc-windows-msvc)

Integration & workflows
- Pipeline-friendly: can export text/json/csv for grep, jq, Python, etc.
- Clipboard integration: copy views or search results from the TUI.
- Packaged for distros and community package managers (Debian, Arch, Nix, Conda, AUR).
- Can extract images to a directory and supports terminal-image debugging.

調研完成。你這台機器其實已經裝了大半的關鍵工具(`pandoc` / `visidata` / `glow` / `bat` / `yazi` / `tv`),缺的主要是一個真正好用的 **Word terminal-native viewer**。以下是 2025–2026 的 best practice 與落地建議。

## 一句話結論

沒有單一工具能「快速看所有 Office 檔」。Best practice 是**按格式分工 + 分兩種情境**(快速 glance vs. 互動閱讀),再用一個 wrapper/yazi previewer 統一入口。

| 格式 | 互動閱讀(TUI) | 快速預覽(stdout,給 yazi/tv/fzf) |
|---|---|---|
| Word `.docx` | **doxx**(terminal-native,最佳) | `doxx --export markdown` → `glow` |
| Excel `.xlsx` | **visidata**(你已裝,直接開) | `xlsx2csv`/`vd -b` → `bat` |
| PowerPoint `.pptx` | 弱項,無原生 TUI | **markitdown** 或 libreoffice 轉檔 |
| 舊版 `.doc/.xls/.ppt`(binary) | 先轉再看 | **libreoffice --headless --convert-to** |
| 通用 fallback / 什麼都能吃 | — | **markitdown**(→ md)/ libreoffice(→ pdf/txt/html) |

## 三層工具地圖

**1. Terminal-native viewer(首選,無需轉檔)**
- **[doxx](https://github.com/bgreenwell/doxx)** — 這次調研最亮眼的工具。純 terminal 的 `.docx` viewer,保留粗體/表格/清單/LaTeX 公式,甚至用 Kitty/iTerm2/Sixel 內嵌圖片;內建搜尋、outline 導航、vim/less keymap,並能 `--export` 成 markdown/text/csv/json/ansi(可接 grep/jq)。`brew install bgreenwell/tap/doxx` 或 `cargo install doxx`。**只吃 `.docx`**。
- **[visidata](https://www.visidata.org/)**(你已裝 `vd`)— `.xlsx/.csv/.parquet/.sqlite/.json` 全能表格多工具,vim 鍵位。看 Excel 直接 `vd file.xlsx`。

**2. 轉檔再 render(快速 glance 的主力)**
- **[pandoc](https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html)**(已裝)— `pandoc file.docx -t gfm | glow -`。⚠️ **重點坑**:pandoc 能讀 `.docx`,但**讀不了 `.pptx` 或 `.xlsx`**(它只能「輸出」pptx)。別拿它處理簡報/試算表。
- **[Microsoft MarkItDown](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown)** — docx/xlsx/**pptx**/pdf 全部 → markdown,LLM-friendly。這是唯一能一鍵吃下 pptx 的輕量 CLI,也是餵給 agent/RAG 的好選擇。`uv tool install markitdown`。

**3. 通用 fallback**

### A1. Top-of-file "Tools:" comment (line 3)

### A2. macOS Homebrew tap pattern (workmux — your closest analog)

There are three moving parts on macOS for a tapped formula. **(a)** the `homebrew_tap` task (lines 15-23), **(b)** the tap must be added to the trust loop (lines 25-51), **(c)** the formula name added to the big `homebrew` install list (line 78).

**(a) Tap the formula** — lines 9-23 (diffnav shown for contrast, workmux is the tarball analog):

```yaml
- name: Tap diffnav formula (macOS)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  community.general.homebrew_tap:
    name: dlvhdr/formulae
    state: present

- name: Tap raine/workmux formula (macOS)
  # workmux is a tmux + git-worktree orchestrator with first-class agent
  # status icons (🤖 working / 💬 waiting / ✅ done) rendered into the tmux
  # window list. Coexists with worktrunk (`wt`); see docs/tools/workmux.md
  # for the wt-vs-wm split.
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  community.general.homebrew_tap:
    name: raine/workmux
    state: present
```

**(b) Trust the tap** (Homebrew 6.0 formula-trust gate) — lines 25-51. Note the comment at line 31 explicitly says to keep this loop in sync with the taps above:

```yaml
# Homebrew 6.0 added a formula-trust security gate: `brew install` refuses to
# load formulae from third-party taps until the tap is explicitly trusted
# ("Error: Refusing to load formula <tap>/<formula> from untrusted tap"). The
# homebrew_tap module has no trust parameter, so trust via `brew trust`.
# Idempotent + back-compatible: older Homebrew has no trust concept, so
# `tap-info` won't contain "Untrusted" and the trust task no-ops (no version
# gate needed). Keep this loop in sync with the third-party taps above — add any
# new third-party tap here too. See pitfalls/homebrew-6-refuses-untrusted-tap-formula.md
- name: Check trust state of third-party taps (macOS, Homebrew >= 6.0 formula-trust gate)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  ansible.builtin.command: "brew tap-info {{ item }}"
  loop:
    - dlvhdr/formulae
    - raine/workmux
  register: devtools_tap_info
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false

- name: Trust untrusted third-party taps (macOS)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
    - "'Untrusted' in item.stdout"
  ansible.builtin.command: "brew trust {{ item.item }}"
  loop: "{{ devtools_tap_info.results }}"
  loop_control:
    label: "{{ item.item }}"
  changed_when: true
```

Note for doxx: the tap is `bgreenwell/tap`, so you'd add `name: bgreenwell/tap` in a new `homebrew_tap` task and add `bgreenwell/tap` to the `loop:` list at lines 36-38.

**(c) The macOS brew install loop** — a single `community.general.homebrew` task with a `name:` list, lines 53-123. `workmux` appears at line 78, `pandoc` at line 95. Excerpt:

```yaml
- name: Install developer CLI tools (macOS)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  community.general.homebrew:
    name:
      - bat
      - bats-core
      ...
      - worktrunk
      - workmux          # line 78
      - zellij
      ...
      - television
      - pandoc           # line 95
      - tailspin
      ...
      - actionlint
    state: present
```

The list closes at line 120 (`state: present`). Adding `doxx` for the tap means adding it to this list (like `workmux`).

### A4. Linux GitHub-release-tarball download+extract pattern (workmux — full block, lines 3242-3383)

This is the exact `.tar.gz` pattern to copy for doxx on Linux. Structure: `command --version` idempotency check → `block:` guarded by `rc != 0` and architecture → mkdir `~/.local/bin` → `uri` GitHub API latest release → arch mapping `set_fact` → build download URL by `selectattr` on asset name → `get_url` to `/tmp` → mkdir temp → `ansible.builtin.unarchive` → `find` binary → `fail` if not found → `copy` to `~/.local/bin` → cleanup, all wrapped in `rescue:`.

```yaml
# --- workmux (tmux + git-worktree orchestrator with agent status icons) ---
# Coexists with worktrunk (`wt`); see docs/tools/workmux.md.
# Releases ship plain `.tar.gz` (NOT `.tar.xz` like worktrunk), so no xz dep.
- name: Check if workmux is installed
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
  ansible.builtin.command: wm --version
  register: workmux_check
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false
  environment:
    PATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"

- name: Install workmux from GitHub releases (Debian/Ubuntu, user-level)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - workmux_check.rc != 0
    - target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64', 'aarch64', 'arm64']
  block:
    - name: Ensure ~/.local/bin exists (workmux)
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
        state: directory
        mode: '0755'

    - name: Get latest workmux release
      ansible.builtin.uri:
        url: https://api.github.com/repos/raine/workmux/releases/latest
        return_content: true
      register: workmux_release

    - name: Set workmux architecture mapping
      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
        workmux_arch: >-
          {{
            'amd64' if target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
            else 'arm64' if target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
            else ''
          }}

    - name: Skip workmux on unsupported architecture
      when: workmux_arch | trim == ''
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: "workmux skipped: no release for {{ target_architecture }}"

    - name: Set workmux download URL fact
      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
        workmux_download_url: >-
          {{
            (
              workmux_release.json.assets
              | selectattr('name', 'equalto', 'workmux-linux-' ~ workmux_arch ~ '.tar.gz')
              | map(attribute='browser_download_url')
              | first
            )
            | default('', true)
          }}

    - name: Skip workmux if download URL could not be determined
      when: workmux_download_url | trim == ''
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: "workmux skipped: could not determine download URL for architecture {{ workmux_arch }}"

    - name: Download workmux tarball
      when: workmux_download_url | trim != ''
      ansible.builtin.get_url:
        url: "{{ workmux_download_url }}"
        dest: /tmp/workmux.tar.gz
        mode: '0644'
        timeout: 120
      retries: 3
      delay: 5

    - name: Create workmux temp directory
      when: workmux_download_url | trim != ''
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: /tmp/workmux
        state: directory
        mode: '0755'

    - name: Extract workmux
      when: workmux_download_url | trim != ''
      ansible.builtin.unarchive:
        src: /tmp/workmux.tar.gz
        dest: /tmp/workmux
        remote_src: true

    - name: Find workmux binary
      when: workmux_download_url | trim != ''
      ansible.builtin.find:
        paths: /tmp/workmux
        patterns: workmux
        file_type: file
        recurse: true
      register: workmux_find

    - name: Fail if workmux binary was not found in extracted archive
      when:
        - workmux_download_url | trim != ''
        - workmux_find.matched | default(0) | int == 0
      ansible.builtin.fail:
        msg: "workmux binary not found under /tmp/workmux after extraction"

    - name: Install workmux to ~/.local/bin
      when:
        - workmux_download_url | trim != ''
        - workmux_find.matched | default(0) | int > 0
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        src: "{{ workmux_find.files[0].path }}"
        dest: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/workmux"
        mode: '0755'
        remote_src: true

    - name: Symlink wm -> workmux for short alias
      when:
        - workmux_download_url | trim != ''
        - workmux_find.matched | default(0) | int > 0
      ansible.builtin.file:
        src: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/workmux"
        dest: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/wm"
        state: link
        force: true

    - name: Clean up workmux temp files
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ item }}"
        state: absent
      loop:
        - /tmp/workmux.tar.gz
        - /tmp/workmux

  rescue:
    - name: Warn workmux installation failed
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: "workmux installation failed (likely network timeout) - skipping"

    - name: Clean up workmux temp files after failure
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ item }}"
        state: absent
      loop:
        - /tmp/workmux.tar.gz
        - /tmp/workmux
```

### A5. Idempotency / `creates:` guards, and unarchive-vs-unzip

**Idempotency guard style (devtools uses `command --version` + `rc != 0`, NOT `creates:`):** Linux tool tasks register a `<tool>_check` from `<tool> --version` with `changed_when: false` / `failed_when: false`, then gate the install `block:` on `<tool>_check.rc != 0` (workmux lines 3245-3257; herdr lines 4294-4306). The `--version` probe runs with an `environment: PATH` that prepends `~/.local/bin` so a prior user-level install is seen.

**`.tar.gz` → `ansible.builtin.unarchive` (confirmed):** The workmux Linux extract (lines 3321-3326) uses `ansible.builtin.unarchive` with `remote_src: true`. This is safe re: the BSD-tar pitfall because the whole block is guarded `when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"` (line 3246/3256) — it only ever runs on Linux (GNU tar). The macOS side never extracts a tarball; it goes through Homebrew. This matches your memory note. The herdr comment at line 4291 explicitly states the single-binary path "sidesteps the macOS BSD-tar .tar.gz pitfall entirely" — reinforcing that `.tar.gz` extraction is deliberately Linux-only here.

**`.zip` → NOT `ansible.builtin.unzip`; they shell out to Python's zipfile.** For zip assets (duckdb, rclone, yazi, lnav) the repo avoids a system `unzip` dependency by running `python3 -m zipfile -e <file.zip> <dest>` via `ansible.builtin.shell` (e.g. rclone line 2061, yazi line 2306, lnav line 3664). Relevant since doxx Linux ships `.tar.gz`, so you want the `unarchive` path (workmux), not these. There is also a `.gz` single-file case (taplo) that uses `gunzip -f` at line 3435.

**Single static binary (no archive) alternative — herdr, lines 4287-4370:** If doxx's Linux release were a bare binary you'd copy this, but doxx ships a tarball, so workmux is the right template. Included for completeness — herdr does `get_url` straight to `~/.local/bin/herdr` with `mode: '0755'` (lines 4357-4365), no unarchive.

Note on doxx Linux asset naming: your tarball is `doxx-$(uname -s)-$(uname -m).tar.gz` → on Linux that resolves to `doxx-Linux-x86_64.tar.gz` / `doxx-Linux-aarch64.tar.gz` (capital "Linux", raw `uname -m` arch). So in the `selectattr('name', 'equalto', ...)` you'd map arch to `x86_64`/`aarch64` (like herdr's mapping at lines 4315-4322, which keeps `x86_64`/`aarch64`), not to `amd64`/`arm64` (workmux's mapping). The workmux block gives the tarball extract mechanics; the herdr block gives the correct `x86_64`/`aarch64` arch mapping — you'd combine them.

## B) `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml` (105 lines)

### B1. Top-of-file comment — schema doc, NOT a tool list

Lines 1-28 are a detailed **schema** comment (documenting each per-entry key), not a flat "Tools:" list like devtools has. There is no separate one-line tool inventory to update here; you just append an entry to the `python_uv_tools:` list. The schema comment:

```yaml
---
# Python CLI tools installed via uv tool install
# Each tool has:
#   - name: package name (can include extras like [cli])
#   - binary: executable name to check for idempotency
#   - with: (optional) additional dependency to install with --with
#   - with_executables_from: (optional) list of packages to install AND
#     expose their entry points in ~/.local/bin (e.g. jupyter-core to get
#     the `jupyter` meta-CLI; `notebook` to get `jupyter-notebook`)
#     NOTE: requires uv >= 0.8.5 (--with-executables-from added in that release)
#     For the meta-CLI dispatch model + the 8 jupyter binaries this exposes,
#     see docs/tools/notebooks.md "The `jupyter` meta-CLI vs standalone binaries".
#     For the auto-upgrade dispatch when uv is too old, see docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md.
#   - extra_binaries: (optional) list of additional binary names that must
#     also exist in ~/.local/bin for the install to be considered complete.
#     Use this whenever `with_executables_from` is set, so adding a new
#     entry-point package later triggers a `--force` reinstall on machines
#     that already have `binary` present from a prior apply. Without this,
#     ansible's `creates:` guard short-circuits the install command and the
#     new exec shims are never written. See
#     pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md.
#   - python: (optional) pin Python version (e.g. "3.11" for thefuck)
#   - needs_modern_gcc: (optional, default false) tool transitively pulls
#     numpy 2.x / pandas 3.x / pyarrow which require GCC ≥ 9.3 to compile
#     from source. Skipped on systems where GCC < 9 (e.g. CentOS 7's
#     gcc 4.8.5). uv falls back to source build because numpy 2.x
#     dropped manylinux_2_17 wheels — see
#     pitfalls/centos7-numpy-pandas-source-build.md.
```

### B2. The `visidata` entry + neighbors (schema examples)

`visidata` — lines 54-64. Note `binary:` differs from `name:` (`vd` vs `visidata`), plus `needs_modern_gcc` and `with:`:

```yaml
  - name: visidata
    binary: vd
    needs_modern_gcc: true  # explicit pandas + pyarrow deps
    with:
      - pandas
      - pyarrow  # Required for parquet/feather/arrow loaders. Note: .feather
                 # files whose schema metadata marks columns as pandas
                 # StringDtype still crash the default PandasSheet path even
                 # with pyarrow installed; the dot_visidatarc override
                 # routes .feather → ArrowSheet to dodge that. See
                 # pitfalls/visidata-feather-stringdtype-numpy-dtype.md.
```

Simplest possible entries (this is what a plain `markitdown` would look like — `name` == package, `binary` == executable, nothing else) — lines 31-53:

```yaml
python_uv_tools:
  - name: thefuck
    binary: thefuck
    python: "3.11"  # Python 3.13 removed distutils which thefuck still uses
  - name: apprise
    binary: apprise
  - name: sqlit-tui[ssh]
    binary: sqlit
    needs_modern_gcc: true  # textual-fastdatatable -> pandas -> numpy 2.x
    with:
      - psycopg2-binary
      - pymysql
      - mssql-python
      - pyodbc
      - duckdb
  - name: python-dotenv[cli]
    binary: dotenv
  - name: git-filter-repo
    binary: git-filter-repo
  - name: mlflow
    binary: mlflow
    needs_modern_gcc: true  # sqlalchemy -> greenlet C++ ext needs proper C++11 (CentOS 7 gcc 4.8.5 lacks it by default)
  - name: tmuxp
    binary: tmuxp
```

For `markitdown` (`uv tool install markitdown`, binary `markitdown`, pure-Python), the two-line form (`name:` / `binary:` like `apprise` or `tmuxp`) is the exact analog. It does not need `with`, `python`, `needs_modern_gcc`, `with_executables_from`, or `extra_binaries`.

### B3. The only entry using `with_executables_from` + `extra_binaries` together (jupyterlab) — lines 74-87

Confirms the CLAUDE.md rule that the two keys co-occur:

```yaml
  - name: jupyterlab
    binary: jupyter-lab
    needs_modern_gcc: true  # ipykernel -> pyzmq -> Cython-generated C99 (gcc 4.8.5 defaults to gnu89); also marimo[sandbox]/[recommended] chains can pull pyarrow

      - ipykernel

    with_executables_from:

      - jupyter-core   # exposes the `jupyter` meta-CLI dispatcher
    extra_binaries:

      - jupyter-notebook  # from notebook
```

(markitdown needs neither of these — single package, single `markitdown` entry point.)

## C) `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/tasks/main.yml` (248 lines) — how entries are consumed

The install loop is a single `ansible.builtin.command` templating `uv tool install` flags, looping over `python_uv_tools`. There is no `creates:`; idempotency is done via a pre-probe `stat` of extra_binaries plus a `_primary_exists` path check, combined in `when:` / `changed_when:`.

**Pre-probe of extra_binaries** — lines 193-202:

```yaml
- name: Probe extra_binaries presence (for entries using with_executables_from)
  ansible.builtin.stat:
    path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/{{ item.1 }}"
  loop: >-
    {{ python_uv_tools
       | subelements('extra_binaries', skip_missing=True) }}
  loop_control:
    label: "{{ item.0.name }} -> {{ item.1 }}"
  register: _uv_extra_binaries_probe
  changed_when: false
```

**The install task** — lines 204-249. Note the flag templating (lines 205-211): `--force` when extras missing, then `{{ item.name }}`, then optional `--python`, `--with`, and `--with-executables-from` loops. The idempotency logic lives in `vars:` (`_missing_extras`, `_force_reinstall`, `_primary_exists`), `changed_when:` (line 236), and `when:` (lines 240-242):

```yaml
- name: Install Python CLI tools via uv
  ansible.builtin.command: >-
    uv tool install
    {% if _force_reinstall %}--force {% endif %}
    {{ item.name }}
    {% if item.python is defined %}--python {{ item.python }} {% endif %}
    {% if item.with is defined %}{% for dep in item.with %}--with {{ dep }} {% endfor %}{% endif %}
    {% if item.with_executables_from is defined %}{% for dep in item.with_executables_from %}--with-executables-from {{ dep }} {% endfor %}{% endif %}
  vars:
    # True when ANY declared extra_binary is missing on disk. We can't use
    # `creates:` for these entries because the primary `binary` may already
    # exist from a previous apply (before `with_executables_from` was added
    # or extended), causing ansible to skip the command and never write the
    # new shims. See pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md.
    _extras: "{{ item.extra_binaries | default([]) }}"
    _missing_extras: >-
      {{ _uv_extra_binaries_probe.results
         | default([])
         | selectattr('item.0.name', 'equalto', item.name)
         | rejectattr('stat.exists')
         | map(attribute='item.1')
         | list }}
    _force_reinstall: "{{ _missing_extras | length > 0 }}"
    _primary_binary_path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/{{ item.binary }}"
    _primary_exists: "{{ _primary_binary_path is exists }}"
  register: python_uv_tool_install
  until: python_uv_tool_install is succeeded

  environment:

    UV_HTTP_RETRIES: "5"

    - not (item.needs_modern_gcc | default(false) and gcc_too_old)
    - (not _primary_exists) or _force_reinstall
  loop: "{{ python_uv_tools }}"
  loop_control:

      {{ item.name

### B1. Inventory of `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_*`

### B2. Best template for a Python self-bootstrapping uv tool

Two are directly relevant. **`executable_pqsum` is the best single-file argparse template** (self-contained, PEP723, argparse dispatch). **`executable_yth` is the best umbrella-dispatcher template** (thin launcher that imports `scripts/<name>/*` leaf modules and execs other tools). Both share the identical self-boot header.

**Self-boot shebang + PEP723 header (identical in `executable_pqsum`, `executable_yth`, `executable_mlf`):**
```python
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --quiet --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = [
#   "rich>=13.9",
# ]
# ///
```
`executable_yth` header (shows a richer dependency block):
```python
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --quiet --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = [
#   "yt-dlp>=2025.1",
#   "tyro>=0.9",
#   "rich>=13.9",
#   "platformdirs>=4",
# ]
# ///
```
The shebang `#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --quiet --script` is the self-bootstrap mechanism — uv reads the inline `# /// script` metadata, builds an ephemeral venv with those deps, and runs the file. No separate install step. (chezmoi's `executable_` prefix makes the deployed file `+x`.)

**Argument parsing / dispatch — `executable_pqsum` uses `argparse`** (imported at line 45). `executable_yth` hand-rolls a positional dispatcher (no argparse at the umbrella level; each leaf module owns its own `tyro` parsing). Neither uses click. The two dispatch styles:

`executable_yth` (umbrella → leaf-module dispatch), lines 147-190:
```python
def main() -> int:
    # Help paths print USAGE and exit BEFORE any heavy import
    if len(sys.argv) >= 2 and sys.argv[1] in ("-h", "--help", "help"):
        print(USAGE)
        return 0

    src = _source_path()
    if str(src) not in sys.path:
        sys.path.insert(0, str(src))

    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        return _dispatch_tv([])          # bare `yth` → tv picker

    sub = sys.argv[1]
    rest = sys.argv[2:]

    leaves = {
        "import-takeout": ("import_takeout", "yth import-takeout"),
        "sync": ("sync", "yth sync"),
        "search": ("search", "yth search"),
        "list": ("list", "yth list"),
        "show": ("show", "yth show"),
    }
    if sub in leaves:
        module, prog = leaves[sub]
        return _leaf(module, prog, rest)

    shims = {"open": _dispatch_open, "copy": _dispatch_copy, "play": _dispatch_play}
    if sub in shims:
        return shims[sub](rest)
    if sub == "tv":
        return _dispatch_tv(rest)

    print(f"yth: unknown subcommand '{sub}'\n\n{USAGE}", file=sys.stderr)
    return 2

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```
The leaf-handoff helper (rewrites argv, imports the module, calls its tyro `main()`), lines 113-117:
```python
def _leaf(module: str, prog: str, args: list[str]) -> int:
    sys.argv = [prog, *args]
    mod = __import__(f"scripts.yth.{module}", fromlist=["main"])
    return mod.main()
```

### B3. How the wrapper finds/execs other tools and handles PATH

**Two idioms in `executable_yth`:**

1. **Locate the chezmoi source dir** so leaf modules under `scripts/<name>/` are importable (lines 71-97):
```python
def _source_path() -> Path:
    chezmoi = shutil.which("chezmoi")
    if chezmoi:
        try:
            out = subprocess.run(
                [chezmoi, "source-path"],
                capture_output=True, text=True, check=False, timeout=5,
            )
            if out.returncode == 0 and out.stdout.strip():
                return Path(out.stdout.strip())
        except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError):
            pass
    fallback = Path.home() / ".local" / "share" / "chezmoi"
    if (fallback / "scripts" / "yth" / "__init__.py").is_file():
        return fallback
    print("yth: cannot locate chezmoi source dir. ...", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(2)
```
This is called out in yth's docstring as "Identical strategy to `executable_mlf:_source_path` / `executable_fleet`."

2. **Find + exec another tool via `shutil.which` + `os.execvp`** (replaces the process so signals propagate), lines 100-110:
```python
def _dispatch_tv(args: list[str]) -> int:
    tv = shutil.which("tv")
    if not tv:
        print("yth: `tv` (television) not in PATH — ...", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    os.execvp(tv, [tv, "yth", *args])
```

**`executable_pqsum`** finds AI CLIs by bare name in `subprocess`/`shutil.which` calls; its `AGENT_CONFIG` dict (lines 123-129) maps agent → argv-prefix (`["opencode","run",...]`, `["claude","-p",...]`, etc.), relying on inherited PATH. Neither launcher hard-codes PATH augmentation — that PATH-prelude pattern lives only in `scripts/fleet/pueue.py:_REMOTE_CMD` / `scripts/fleet/exec.py:_PATH_PRELUDE` (per CLAUDE.md), which is for *remote/cron* contexts, not local launchers. For a local `view-office` wrapper, the yth `shutil.which` + `os.execvp` pattern is the one to copy.

Note `executable_pqsum` also demonstrates the shared-SSOT loader pattern (lines 72-96) reading `~/.config/shell/04_ai_agents.sh` — only relevant if your tool needs AI config; a plain office viewer does not.

### C1. The two-file hand-written pattern (Strategy B eager-load)

Completions live in two separate directories, one file per shell, **eager-sourced** at shell startup (not lazy `~/.zfunc` autoload). Both guard on the command existing, then register.

**zsh file** — `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/zsh/tools/48_pqsum_completion.zsh` (verbatim):
```zsh
# 48_pqsum_completion.zsh - tab completion for `pqsum` (pueue queue summary).
(( $+commands[pqsum] )) || return 0

_pqsum() {
    local context state state_descr line
    typeset -A opt_args

    _arguments -C \
        '(- *)'{-h,--help}'[show help]' \
        '(-g --group)'{-g,--group}'=[restrict to one pueue group]:group:->group' \
        '--report[emit markdown report (ai mode only)]' \
        '--out=[write report to PATH]:path:_files' \
        ...
        '1:mode:(text ai json)'

    case "$state" in
        group)
            local -a groups
            if (( $+commands[pueue] )) && (( $+commands[jq] )); then
                groups=( ${(f)"$(pueue status --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.groups | keys[]' 2>/dev/null)"} )
                (( ${#groups} )) && _describe 'pueue group' groups
            fi
            ;;
    esac
}

compdef _pqsum pqsum
```

**bash file** — `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/bash/48_pqsum_completion.bash` (verbatim):
```bash
# 48_pqsum_completion.bash - tab completion for `pqsum` (pueue queue summary).
command -v pqsum >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0

_pqsum_completion() {
    local cur prev words cword
    _init_completion -n = || return

    case "$prev" in
        -g|--group)
            if command -v pueue >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                local groups
                groups=$(pueue status --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.groups | keys[]' 2>/dev/null)
                COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "$groups" -- "$cur") )
            fi
            return ;;
        --out) _filedir; return ;;
    esac

    case "$cur" in
        -*)
            local opts="-h --help -g --group --report --out --clean ..."
            COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "$opts" -- "$cur") ) ;;
        *)
            # positional (mode) counting ...
            COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "text ai json" -- "$cur") ) ;;
    esac
}

complete -F _pqsum_completion pqsum
```

docs/shells/aliases.md:612:> VisiData ([`visidata.org`](https://www.visidata.org/)) — terminal spreadsheet for tabular data (CSV/TSV/JSON/parquet/feather/arrow/xlsx/sqlite). Defaults are already vim-flavored (h/j/k/l, gg/G, /? search). Companion rc at `~/.visidatarc` (chezmoi-managed via [`dot_visidatarc.tmpl`](../../dot_visidatarc.tmpl)) carries the feather/StringDtype workaround and `enableVimMode`-gated key rebinds — see [vim-mode.md → VisiData](../this_repo/vim-mode.md#visidata).
docs/shells/aliases.md:616:| `vd-arrow` | alias | `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh` | `visidata -f arrow` — force the pure-pyarrow ArrowSheet loader. Escape hatch for `.feather` / `.arrow` files where the default PandasSheet path crashes on pandas `StringDtype` columns (`ValueError: Could not convert ... to NumPy dtype`). Full diagnosis: [pitfalls/visidata-feather-stringdtype-numpy-dtype.md](../../pitfalls/visidata-feather-stringdtype-numpy-dtype.md) |
docs/shells/aliases.md:617:| `vd-ro` | alias | `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh` | `visidata --readonly` — open in read-only mode so a stray `g Ctrl+S` cannot overwrite the source. `--readonly` is an optalias for `--overwrite=n` (`visidata/modify.py:11`); in-memory edits are still allowed but the save path fails. Pair with `vd-arrow` (e.g. `visidata --readonly -f arrow file.feather`) when both protections are wanted. See [vim-mode.md → VisiData → Data safety](../this_repo/vim-mode.md#data-safety-read-only-mode) |

# chezmoi-dotfiles

This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** (configs) + **ansible** (system
deps) dotfiles repo. This skill is the agent-facing map: how to drive it, and what
custom tooling exists that you wouldn't otherwise know about. It is rendered per-host
— the "What's enabled on THIS machine" section reflects what the user actually
selected at init.

## Orientation (read this first)

- **Repo root**: `chezmoi source-path` (no args) prints the source dir. Work there
  to edit: `cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`.
- **Source path of one file**: `chezmoi source-path ~/.config/foo/bar` → the
  managed source file for that target.
- **`docs/**` is NOT deployed to `$HOME`** (it's chezmoi-ignored). Read detail via
  `"$(chezmoi source-path)/docs/..."`. A *subset* is deployed to `~/.config/docs/`
  (e.g. keybindings, cli-tools) for runtime helpers.
- **Read the contract before editing**: `"$(chezmoi source-path)/CLAUDE.md"` holds
  Hard invariants and cross-file maintenance rules. Honor them.
- This host: profile `macos_intel`, OS `darwin`/`amd64`, primary shell `zsh`.

## chezmoi essentials

```bash
chezmoi diff                 # preview changes (also: just chezmoi-diff)
chezmoi apply                # deploy + run scripts (also: cas, or just chezmoi-apply)
chezmoi status               # modified/added/removed targets
chezmoi edit ~/.zshrc        # edit the SOURCE of a target
chezmoi add  ~/.config/x     # start managing an existing file
chezmoi re-add               # pull live edits back into source
chezmoi managed | grep foo   # is X managed?
chezmoi cat ~/.config/x      # render a target without applying
chezmoi data | jq            # the template data (ground truth for the toggles below)
```

- **`cas`** = `chezmoi apply` + reload hint; **`cau`** = update from remote then apply
  (defined in `dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh`).
- **`dotcfg`** = reconfigure the init prompts on an already-set-up machine
  (`dotcfg` for the TUI, `dotcfg --set installLlmTools=true --yes` for one toggle,
  `dotcfg --dry-run` to preview). Shell twin: `czcfg`.
- **Never `chezmoi add` a `modify_`/`create_` target** — it overwrites the script.
- Full command cheat-sheet: `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`. Install-vs-upgrade is
  split: `chezmoi apply`/ansible is **install-only**; upgrades go through
  `just upgrade-*`.

## What's enabled on THIS machine

(Rendered from this host's selections. For live truth: `chezmoi data | jq`.)
- **Coding agents** — Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor, Codex, Gemini, Copilot (configs + CLIs). See `docs/tools/agent-overlays.md`, `docs/tools/agent-skills.md`.
- **Python uv tools** — mlflow, marimo, jupyter, etc. (powers the `mlf` CLI). See `docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md`.
- **Extra runtimes** — rust, bun, ruby via mise (+ cargo/gem tools). Node is always present.
- **LLM tools** — Ollama / LiteLLM / local models.
- **JS CLI tools** — standalone npm CLIs (e.g. readability-cli).
- **.NET tools** — .NET SDK (mise) + dotnet global tools.
- **IaC** — Azure CLI, Terraform, OpenTofu.
- **Media** — ffmpeg, ImageMagick, exiftool, libvips.
- **Media control** — nowplaying-cli + switchaudio-osx (macOS) / playerctl (Linux); unlocks full `sysplay`/`sysnow` (built-in `sysvol`/`sysmute` work regardless).
- **Networking** — nmap, mtr, httpie, gping, trippy.
- **Tunnels** — ngrok, cloudflared.
- **Vim mode** — shell modal editing + tmux vim nav (NOT Neovim/editors — those are always vim).

## Custom in-house CLIs (always deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin`, on PATH)

Each works from any cwd. Run with `--help`, or read `docs/tools/<name>.md`. Full list: `ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_dotfiles/bin/"`.

- **`fleet`** — cross-host ops over your machines: `fleet chezmoi apply`, `fleet hosts`, `fleet tmux`, `fleet info`, `fleet pueue`, `fleet exec`. See `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-exec.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md`.
- **`mlf`** — MLflow umbrella CLI + TUI dashboard (needs Python uv tools). Picker twin: `tv mlflow`.
- **`pqsum`** — pueue queue summary (text / AI / JSON). See `docs/tools/pueue.md`.
- **`x`** — clipboard/file copy-paste-open with cross-platform fallbacks.
- **`mi-router`** / **`reyee`** / **`sms`** — read-only router CLIs (Xiaomi MiWiFi / Ruijie Reyee / Huawei HiLink SMS). See `docs/tools/{mi-router,reyee,sms}.md`.
- **`mi-dhcp-bind`** — opt-in **write** companion to `mi-router`: set/remove MiWiFi static DHCP reservations (`bind --self` autodetects this host). See `docs/tools/mi-dhcp-bind.md`.
- **`ping-monitor`** — record ping over time, flag latency spikes. See `docs/tools/ping-monitor.md`.
- **`yth`** — search your YouTube watch history (title/channel/description + captions; Takeout import + optional cookie sync). Picker twin: `tv yth`. See `docs/tools/yth.md`.
- **`dotcfg`** — reconfigure dotfiles prompts (above).
- **`sesh-preview`** — preview helper for the sesh picker.

## Television (`tv`) — fuzzy pickers with custom channels

There are ~40 **custom** channels (system state, fleet, services, infra, agents…)
that you won't discover otherwise. Browse them:

```bash
tv                      # default picker
tv list-channels        # list everything available
tv <channel>            # open one, e.g. tv fleet-hosts | tv mlflow | tv pueue
ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_config/television/cable/"   # the channel definitions
```

Handy ones: `fleet-hosts`, `mlflow`, `pueue`, `ports`, `kill-process`, `services`,
`sessions`, `keybindings`, `aliases`, `git-ops`, `mac-apps`/`linux-apps`. Full
reference: `docs/tools/tv.md`.

## Keybindings & keymaps

- **`bindings`** (shell function) or **`tv keybindings`** — interactive reference.
- **tmux**: `prefix + Space` (or `prefix + e`) opens the action menu;
  `prefix + T` = sesh picker, `prefix + U` = tools. Deep ref: `docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md`.
- **shell ZLE widgets**: `Alt+S` sesh sessions, `Alt+T` tools, `Ctrl+R` history (atuin).
- Master reference: `docs/shells/keybindings.md` (also deployed to `~/.config/docs/shells/keybindings.md`).

## Aliases & functions

`alias` to list shell aliases, or `tv aliases`. Catalog: `docs/shells/aliases.md`.
Helpers worth knowing: `chezmoi-cd` (jump to source), `run-for` (time-box a command),
`bindings` (above). App control: `applaunch`/`appquit`/`apprestart`/… (cross-platform).
System audio (cross-platform, built-in): `sysvol`/`sysmute` (+ `sysplay`/`sysnow` with `installMediaControl`); remote mute via `fleet exec --login -- sysmute on`.

## just recipes (run from the source dir)

```bash
cd "$(chezmoi source-path)" && just --list
```

Categories: `chezmoi-*`, `ansible-*`, `upgrade-*` (brew/mise/uv/npm/cargo/…),
`fleet`/`fleet-*`, `gen-prompts` (regenerate prompt scaffolding), `check`/`lint`,
`docker-*`. See `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`.

## Editing rules (don't skip)

Before changing anything under the repo, read `CLAUDE.md` Hard invariants and the
"Cross-file maintenance rules" table — many surfaces have mandatory mirror updates
in the same commit (docs, completions, tool-managers index, this very skill, …).

7	#   - with_executables_from: (optional) list of packages to install AND
8	#     expose their entry points in ~/.local/bin (e.g. jupyter-core to get
9	#     the `jupyter` meta-CLI; `notebook` to get `jupyter-notebook`)

11	#     For the meta-CLI dispatch model + the 8 jupyter binaries this exposes,
12	#     see docs/tools/notebooks.md "The `jupyter` meta-CLI vs standalone binaries".
13	#     For the auto-upgrade dispatch when uv is too old, see docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md.
14	#   - extra_binaries: (optional) list of additional binary names that must
15	#     also exist in ~/.local/bin for the install to be considered complete.
16	#     Use this whenever `with_executables_from` is set, so adding a new
17	#     entry-point package later triggers a `--force` reinstall on machines
18	#     that already have `binary` present from a prior apply. Without this,
19	#     ansible's `creates:` guard short-circuits the install command and the
20	#     new exec shims are never written. See

```text
1	---
2	# Python CLI tools via uv
3	# uv is bootstrapped before ansible runs (run_once_before_00_bootstrap.sh.tmpl
4	# curls the official installer to ~/.local/bin/uv when missing). This role
5	# additionally guarantees that uv is recent enough for the flags it uses.
6	
7	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
8	# Minimum-uv-version gate (auto-upgrade aware)
9	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
10	#
11	# The role's `defaults/main.yml` uses `with_executables_from:` for the
12	# jupyterlab entry to expose `jupyter` / `jupyter-notebook` shims from
13	# jupyter-core / notebook. That is the `--with-executables-from` flag of
14	# `uv tool install`, added in uv 0.8.5 (PR astral-sh/uv#14014, released
15	# 2025-08-xx). Older uv aborts the install loop with:
16	#   error: unexpected argument '--with-executables-from' found
17	#
18	# The user's fleet currently spans:
19	#   * macOS w/ Homebrew uv  → /opt/homebrew/bin/uv         (`brew upgrade uv`)
20	#   * macOS w/ curl install → ~/.local/bin/uv              (`uv self update`)
21	#   * Ubuntu w/ curl install → ~/.local/bin/uv             (`uv self update`)
22	#   * Linuxbrew              → /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/uv (`brew upgrade uv`)
23	#
24	# `uv self update` REFUSES on brew installs ("self-update is disabled for
25	# this build"). So we detect the install style and dispatch to the right
26	# upgrade command rather than blindly trying one. See
27	# `pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md` and
28	# `pitfalls/ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md`.
29	- name: Set minimum required uv version
30	  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
31	    min_uv_version: "0.8.5"
32	
33	# Probe current uv version. `uv --version` prints e.g.:
34	#   "uv 0.7.4 (6fbcd09b5 2025-05-15)"
35	#   "uv 0.10.2 (Homebrew 2026-02-10)"
36	#   "uv 0.7.18"
37	# We take field 2 with awk to avoid `regex_replace` inside `when:` clauses,
38	# which silently strips one layer of backslashes (\S → S, \1 → 1) and makes
39	# the regex never match — `regex_replace` then returns the original string,
40	# and the version test fails with a misleading
41	#   "'<' not supported between instances of 'str' and 'int'".
42	# See pitfalls/ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md.
43	- name: Probe current uv version
44	  ansible.builtin.shell: |
45	    set -e
46	    uv --version | awk '{print $2}'
47	  args:
48	    executable: /bin/bash
49	  register: _uv_initial
50	  changed_when: false
51	
52	- name: Set initial uv_version fact (clean string, safe for `is version()`)
53	  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
54	    _uv_initial_version: "{{ _uv_initial.stdout | trim }}"
55	
56	# Detect install style by binary path + brew formula registry.
57	# Order matters: a path under */homebrew/* or */linuxbrew/* is
58	# unambiguous. /usr/local/bin/uv is shared between Intel-mac brew and the
59	# curl installer — disambiguate by asking brew if it owns the formula.
60	- name: Detect uv install style (brew vs curl-installer vs other)
61	  ansible.builtin.shell: |
62	    set -e
63	    p="$(command -v uv)"
64	    case "$p" in
65	      */homebrew/*|*/Cellar/*|*/linuxbrew/*)
66	        echo brew
67	        ;;
68	      /usr/local/bin/uv)
69	        if command -v brew >/dev/null 2>&1 \
70	           && brew list --formula uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
71	          echo brew
72	        else
73	          echo curl
74	        fi
75	        ;;
76	      "$HOME"/.local/bin/uv|"$HOME"/.cargo/bin/uv)
77	        echo curl
78	        ;;
79	      *)
80	        # Best-effort fallback: if brew owns the formula, treat as brew;
81	        # else assume self-update-capable (curl style or stand-alone binary).
82	        if command -v brew >/dev/null 2>&1 \
83	           && brew list --formula uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
84	          echo brew
85	        else
86	          echo curl
87	        fi
88	        ;;
89	    esac
90	  args:
91	    executable: /bin/bash
92	  register: _uv_install_style
93	  changed_when: false
94	
95	- name: Show detected uv state
96	  ansible.builtin.debug:
97	    msg: >-
98	      uv {{ _uv_initial_version }}
99	      (install style: {{ _uv_install_style.stdout }};
100	      minimum required: {{ min_uv_version }})
101	
102	# --- Upgrade dispatch (only fires when uv is too old) ---
103	
104	# `community.general.homebrew state=latest` is idempotent and runs as the
105	# invoking user (no become). Covers macOS Homebrew + Linuxbrew.
106	- name: Upgrade uv via Homebrew (brew install detected, version too old)
107	  community.general.homebrew:
108	    name: uv
109	    state: latest
110	  when:
111	    - _uv_initial_version is version(min_uv_version, '<')
112	    - _uv_install_style.stdout == 'brew'
113	  register: _uv_brew_upgrade
114	  until: _uv_brew_upgrade is succeeded
115	  retries: 3
116	  delay: 10
117	
118	# `uv self update` is the canonical refresh for the curl/standalone install.
119	# Network-dependent so retried; treat "already up to date" stdout as not-changed.
120	- name: Upgrade uv via self-update (curl install detected, version too old)
121	  ansible.builtin.command: uv self update
122	  register: _uv_self_update
123	  changed_when: >-
124	    'updated to' in (_uv_self_update.stdout | default(''))
125	    or 'updated to' in (_uv_self_update.stderr | default(''))
126	  until: _uv_self_update is succeeded
127	  retries: 3
128	  delay: 10
129	  when:
130	    - _uv_initial_version is version(min_uv_version, '<')
131	    - _uv_install_style.stdout == 'curl'
132	
133	# Re-probe unconditionally — cheap, and gives us a clean post-upgrade fact
134	# regardless of which (or no) upgrade branch fired.
135	- name: Re-probe uv version after upgrade attempt
136	  ansible.builtin.shell: |
137	    set -e
138	    uv --version | awk '{print $2}'
139	  args:
140	    executable: /bin/bash
141	  register: _uv_final
142	  changed_when: false
143	
144	- name: Set final uv_version fact
145	  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
146	    uv_version: "{{ _uv_final.stdout | trim }}"
147	
148	- name: Fail if uv is still too old after auto-upgrade attempt
149	  ansible.builtin.fail:
150	    msg: |
151	      uv {{ uv_version }} is below the required minimum {{ min_uv_version }},
152	      and the auto-upgrade attempt did not help (install style detected:
153	      {{ _uv_install_style.stdout }}).
154	
155	      Manual fix by install style:
156	        macOS Homebrew     →  brew upgrade uv
157	        Linuxbrew          →  brew upgrade uv
158	        curl/standalone    →  uv self update     (or: just upgrade-tools uv)
159	        unknown / other    →  reinstall via https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/
160	
161	      The --with-executables-from flag (used by the jupyterlab entry in
162	      this role's defaults/main.yml) was added in uv 0.8.5
163	      (PR astral-sh/uv#14014).
164	  when: uv_version is version(min_uv_version, '<')
165	
166	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
167	# GCC capability gate (for tools that fall back to source builds)
168	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
169	# Modern wheel ecosystem dropped manylinux_2_17 (CentOS 7 baseline) so older
170	# glibc hosts fall back to compiling numpy / pandas / pyarrow from source —
171	# and the build now requires GCC >= 9.3 (numpy meson build asserts).
172	# CentOS 7 ships gcc 4.8.5; the tools tagged `needs_modern_gcc: true` get
173	# skipped there. See pitfalls/centos7-numpy-pandas-source-build.md.
174	- name: Detect host C compiler (gcc) version
175	  ansible.builtin.shell: |
176	    set -e
177	    if command -v gcc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
178	      gcc -dumpversion 2>/dev/null | head -1
179	    else
180	      echo "0"
181	    fi
182	  args:
183	    executable: /bin/bash
184	  register: gcc_version_probe
185	  changed_when: false
186	  failed_when: false
187	
188	- name: Set fact gcc_too_old (true when major < 9)
189	  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
190	    gcc_too_old: >-
191	      {{ ((gcc_version_probe.stdout | trim).split('.')[0] | int) < 9 }}
192	
193	- name: Probe extra_binaries presence (for entries using with_executables_from)
194	  ansible.builtin.stat:
195	    path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/{{ item.1 }}"
196	  loop: >-
197	    {{ python_uv_tools
198	       | subelements('extra_binaries', skip_missing=True) }}
199	  loop_control:
200	    label: "{{ item.0.name }} -> {{ item.1 }}"
201	  register: _uv_extra_binaries_probe
202	  changed_when: false
203	
204	- name: Install Python CLI tools via uv
205	  ansible.builtin.command: >-
206	    uv tool install
207	    {% if _force_reinstall %}--force {% endif %}
208	    {{ item.name }}
209	    {% if item.python is defined %}--python {{ item.python }} {% endif %}
210	    {% if item.with is defined %}{% for dep in item.with %}--with {{ dep }} {% endfor %}{% endif %}
211	    {% if item.with_executables_from is defined %}{% for dep in item.with_executables_from %}--with-executables-from {{ dep }} {% endfor %}{% endif %}
212	  vars:
213	    # True when ANY declared extra_binary is missing on disk. We can't use
214	    # `creates:` for these entries because the primary `binary` may already
215	    # exist from a previous apply (before `with_executables_from` was added
216	    # or extended), causing ansible to skip the command and never write the
217	    # new shims. See pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md.
218	    _extras: "{{ item.extra_binaries | default([]) }}"
219	    _missing_extras: >-
220	      {{ _uv_extra_binaries_probe.results
221	         | default([])
222	         | selectattr('item.0.name', 'equalto', item.name)
223	         | rejectattr('stat.exists')
224	         | map(attribute='item.1')
225	         | list }}
226	    _force_reinstall: "{{ _missing_extras | length > 0 }}"
227	    _primary_binary_path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/{{ item.binary }}"
228	    _primary_exists: "{{ _primary_binary_path is exists }}"
229	  register: python_uv_tool_install
230	  until: python_uv_tool_install is succeeded
231	  retries: 3
232	  delay: 5
233	  # Skip when:
234	  #   - primary binary already exists, AND
235	  #   - either no extras declared, or all extras already present
236	  changed_when: python_uv_tool_install.rc == 0 and (_force_reinstall or not _primary_exists)
237	  environment:
238	    UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT: "120"
239	    UV_HTTP_RETRIES: "5"
240	  when:
241	    - not (item.needs_modern_gcc | default(false) and gcc_too_old)
242	    - (not _primary_exists) or _force_reinstall
243	  loop: "{{ python_uv_tools }}"
244	  loop_control:
245	    label: >-
246	      {{ item.name
247	         }}{% if item.needs_modern_gcc | default(false) and gcc_too_old %} [SKIPPED: needs gcc >= 9]{% endif
248	         %}{% if item.extra_binaries is defined %} [extras: {{ item.extra_binaries | join(',') }}]{% endif %}

# ~/.config/yazi/yazi.toml
# Yazi configuration (tested with v0.3.3+, syntax updated for v25.12.29+)
# Last updated: 2026-02-12
# Documentation: https://yazi-rs.github.io/docs/configuration/yazi/
# Default preset: https://github.com/sxyazi/yazi/blob/shipped/yazi-config/preset/yazi.toml

[manager]
ratio = [1, 4, 3]           # Layout: 1/8 parent, 4/8 current, 3/8 preview
sort_by = "natural"          # Natural number sorting
sort_dir_first = true        # Show directories first
linemode = "size"            # Show file sizes by default
show_hidden = true           # Show hidden files
show_symlink = true          # Show symlink targets

# -----------------------
# Open rules: 決定 Enter / o 的預設 opener，還有 O 的候選清單
# -----------------------
[open]
rules = [
  # 目錄：提供多種 opener 給 O 選
  # Note: Use url = "*/" for directories (recommended), not mime = "inode/directory"
  { url = "*/", use = ["edit", "git", "marimo_dir", "agent", "open"] },

  # Python 檔：提供 marimo sandbox
  { url = "*.py", use = ["edit", "marimo_py_sandbox", "open", "code"] },

  # 文字/程式碼檔：edit/open/code
  { mime = "text/*", use = ["edit", "open", "code"] },

  # 其他：至少能 open
  { mime = "*", use = ["open"] },
]

# -----------------------
# Openers: 真正的「Open with」選項
# -----------------------
[opener]

# --- edit：nvim，會把 cwd 切到目標（dir）或檔案所在資料夾（file）
edit = [
  { run = """sh -lc '
t="$1"
if [ -d "$t" ]; then
  cd "$t" && exec nvim .
else
  cd "$(dirname "$t")" && exec nvim "$t"
fi
' -- %s1
""", block = true, desc = "Neovim (auto cd into dir)" },
]

# --- open：macOS 預設開啟
open = [
  { run = """sh -lc 'exec open "$1"' -- %s1 """, block = false, desc = "Open (macOS default)" },
  { run = """sh -lc '
t="$1"
if [ -d "$t" ]; then
  cd "$t"
else
  cd "$(dirname "$t")"
fi
[ -f .venv/bin/activate ] && source .venv/bin/activate
# Use ipython from venv if available, otherwise fallback to python
if [ -f .venv/bin/ipython ]; then
  REPL=ipython
elif command -v ipython >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ ! -f .venv/bin/activate ]; then
  # Only use system ipython if no venv is active (to avoid the warning)
  REPL=ipython
else
  REPL=python
fi
if [ -d "$t" ]; then
  exec $REPL
else
  exec $REPL "$t"
fi
' -- %s1
""", block = true, desc = "ipython/python (auto cd, source .venv, fallback to python if no venv ipython)" },
  # BUG: (if ipython not install in the .venv, fallback to python) /Users/daviddwlee84/miniforge3/lib/python3.12/site-packages/IPython/core/interactiveshell.py:937: UserWarning: Attempting to work in a virtualenv. If you encounter problems, please install IPython inside the virtualenv.
#   { run = """sh -lc '
# t="$1"
# if [ -d "$t" ]; then
#   cd "$t"
# else
#   cd "$(dirname "$t")"
# fi
# [ -f .venv/bin/activate ] && source .venv/bin/activate
# if [ -d "$t" ]; then
#   exec ipython
# else
#   exec ipython "$t"
# fi
# ' -- "$1"
# """, block = true, desc = "ipython (auto cd into dir and source .venv if exists)" },
]

# --- code：VS Code / Cursor（留一個就好，或兩個都留）
code = [
  { run = """sh -lc 'exec code "$1"' -- %s1 """, block = false, desc = "VS Code" },
  { run = """sh -lc 'exec cursor "$1"' -- %s1 """, block = false, desc = "Cursor" },
]

agent = [
  { run = """sh -lc '
t="$1"
if [ -d "$t" ]; then
  cd "$t"
else
  cd "$(dirname "$t")"
fi
exec specstory run
' -- %s1
""", block = true, desc = "Claude (specstory)" },
  { run = """sh -lc '
t="$1"
if [ -d "$t" ]; then
  cd "$t"
else
  cd "$(dirname "$t")"
fi
exec specstory run opencode
' -- %s1
""", block = true, desc = "OpenCode (specstory)" },
  { run = """sh -lc '
t="$1"
if [ -d "$t" ]; then
  cd "$t"
else
  cd "$(dirname "$t")"
fi
exec specstory run codex
' -- %s1
""", block = true, desc = "Codex (specstory)" },
  { run = """sh -lc '
t="$1"
if [ -d "$t" ]; then
  cd "$t"
else
  cd "$(dirname "$t")"
fi
exec specstory run cursor
' -- %s1
""", block = true, desc = "Cursor Agent CLI (specstory)" },

]

# --- git：在該目錄（或檔案所在目錄）開 lazygit
git = [
  { run = """sh -lc '
t="$1"
if [ -d "$t" ]; then
  cd "$t"
else
  cd "$(dirname "$t")"
fi
exec lazygit
' -- %s1
""", block = true, desc = "Lazygit (here)" },
]

# --- marimo：對目錄用 marimo edit --watch .
marimo_dir = [
  { run = """sh -lc '
t="$1"
if [ -d "$t" ]; then
  cd "$t"
else
  cd "$(dirname "$t")"
fi
exec marimo edit --watch .
' -- %s1
""", block = true, desc = "Marimo (watch dir)" },
]

# --- marimo sandbox：只給 .py 用，避免對 dir 亂套
marimo_py_sandbox = [
  { run = """sh -lc 'exec marimo edit --watch --sandbox "$1"' -- %s1 """, block = true, desc = "Marimo (watch + sandbox py)" },
]
```

```text
189	#### 2.2 Role-driven brew (formulae + casks)
190	
191	Most CLI formulae land via ansible roles, not the Brewfile. Examples:
192	
193	- `base/tasks/main.yml`: `git`, `git-lfs`, `curl`, `wget`, `ripgrep`, `fd`, `jq`, `tree`, `just`
194	- `devtools/tasks/main.yml`: large set — `bat`, `gh`, `glab`, `diffnav`, `git-delta`, `eza`, `tlrc`, `glow`, `gum`, `vhs`, `freeze`, `thefuck`, `zoxide`, `direnv`, `yazi`, `superfile`, `tmux`, `sesh`, `worktrunk`, `workmux`, `zellij`, `btop`, `htop`, `duckdb`, `rclone`, `coreutils`, `taplo`, `television`, `pandoc`, `tailspin`, `lnav`, `grc`, `dasel`, `yq`, `jnv`, `witr`, `figlet`, `toilet`, `lolcat`, `fastfetch`, `shellcheck`, `shfmt`, `bats-core`, `git-graph`, `mosh`
195	- `coding_agents/tasks/main.yml`: `claude-code` (cask), `codex` (cask), `gemini-cli` (formula), `rtk` (formula), `specstory`, `codexbar`, `td`, `sidecar` (all with tap setup)
196	- `networking_tools/`: `nmap`, `arp-scan`, `mtr`, `iperf3`, `doggo`, `httpie`, `gping`, `trippy`, `bandwhich`, `rustscan`, `speedtest` (tap `teamookla/speedtest`), `ngrok`, `cloudflared`
197	- `media_tools/`: `ffmpeg`, `imagemagick`, `exiftool`, `vips`
198	- `iac_tools/`: `azure-cli`, `hashicorp/tap/terraform`, `opentofu`
199	- `llm_tools/`: `llmfit`, `models`, `ollama`
200	- `security_tools/`: `gitleaks`
201	- `starship/`, `atuin/`, `neovim/`, `bash/` (gawk), `zsh/` — each installs its primary tool via homebrew formula on macOS
202	- `pueue` (from `rust_cargo_tools/`): macOS uses homebrew formula
203	
204	**Per-OS dispatch** is the universal pattern in roles: macOS branch uses
205	`community.general.homebrew` / `homebrew_cask`; Linux branches use apt,
206	Linuxbrew (when present), or GitHub releases. See each role for the
207	explicit `when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"` guard.
208	
209	**Tap inventory** (added by various roles): `nikitabobko/tap`,
210	`wxtsky/tap` (CodeIsland), `hashicorp/tap` (terraform),
211	`teamookla/speedtest`, `specstoryai/tap`, `steipete/tap` (CodexBar),
212	`marcus/tap` (td, sidecar), `dlvhdr/formulae`, `raine/workmux`.
213	
214	Homebrew 6+ refuses formulae/casks from untrusted third-party taps. Role-driven
215	taps must run a `brew tap-info <tap>` → `brew trust <tap>` check before installing
216	from that tap; Brewfile taps are handled by the brew-bundle run-script before it
217	calls `brew bundle`. See
218	[`pitfalls/homebrew-6-refuses-untrusted-tap-formula.md`](../../pitfalls/homebrew-6-refuses-untrusted-tap-formula.md).
219	
220	**Adding via homebrew**: prefer a brew formula/cask only when the tool
221	is macOS-shipped and Linux equivalents go via apt or release tarball.
222	Linux-first tools rarely belong in the Brewfile.
223	
224	#### 2.3 Homebrew prefix dispatch helper
225	
226	`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh::_uv_install_style` (and mirrored helpers in
227	`python_uv_tools/tasks/main.yml`) inspect whether a binary lives under
228	`brew --prefix` to decide between `brew upgrade <pkg>` and the tool's
229	native self-update. This avoids the "I `uv self update` on a brew-uv
230	host and silently no-op" trap — see
231	[`pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md).
232	
233	### 3. Ansible roles
234	
235	26 roles under `dot_ansible/roles/`. Triggered by
236	`.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl`
237	(re-runs when any role's `tasks/main.yml` or `defaults/main.yml` changes
238	— SHA256-tracked).
239	
240	**Universal patterns**:
241	
242	- `state: present` / `creates:` — install-only, no silent upgrades
243	- Per-OS branching via `when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"` (or `["Debian", "RedHat"]`)
244	- `tags: [sudo]` on any `become: true` task (so noRoot mode skips them — see [`pitfalls/ansible-missing-sudo-tag.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/ansible-missing-sudo-tag.md))
245	- `failed_when: false` + `register:` for "is the tool installed?" probes
246	- Linux user-level fallback to `~/.local/bin` when distro package is missing or too old (handles RHEL/CentOS + noRoot + Apple-Silicon-not-bottled scenarios)
247	
248	**Role feature flags** (set in `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` via prompts):
249	`installBrewApps`, `installAiDesktopApps`, `installCodingAgents`,
250	`installLlmTools`, `installPythonUvTools`, `installJsCliTools`,
251	`installDotnetTools`, `installIacTools`, `installMediaTools`,
252	`installNetworkingTools`, `installTunnelTools`, `installBitwarden`,
253	`installGamingApps`, `installInputMethod`, `installAuditd`. Roles gate themselves on the
254	matching flag; the bundle script `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py` defines
255	profile presets (`minimal`, `cloud-vm` planned, default-developer, …).
256

Never hand-edit the generated marker regions. | `just gen-prompts -- --check` / the `dotfiles-init-gen-check` pre-commit hook fail on drift; `doctor` is a back-compat alias for `gen --check`. |

1	#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --quiet --script
2	# /// script
3	# requires-python = ">=3.11"
4	# dependencies = [
5	#   "yt-dlp>=2025.1",

7	#   "rich>=13.9",

10	# ///
11	"""yth — search your own YouTube watch history from the terminal.
12	
13	Bare `yth` (no args) launches the `tv yth` fuzzy picker over your history.
14	Subcommands below bypass it for scripted / one-shot use.
15	
16	Subcommands:
17	  import-takeout <file>          Backfill history from a Google Takeout
18	                                 watch-history.json (primary, cookie-free).
19	  sync                           Incremental sync of recent history via
20	                                 yt-dlp :ythistory (needs login cookies).
21	  enrich [--limit N | --all]     Fill missing description/duration/upload_date
22	                                 for videos (yt-dlp; cookie-free for public).
23	  fetch-subs <id>… | --recent N  Download + index subtitle text (auto+manual).
24	             | --all
25	  search <query> [--subs]        FTS5 search over title/channel/description
26	         [--json] [--limit N]    (add --subs to also match caption text).
27	  list [--tsv] [--limit N]       All history, newest first (--tsv feeds tv).
28	  show <id> [--json]             Detail for one video (DB-only, no network).
29	  open <id> | copy <id>          Open in browser / copy URL to clipboard.
30	  play <id>                      mpv if configured+installed, else browser.
31	
32	Data lives in a local sqlite DB (platformdirs user_data_dir/yth/history.db).
33	Cookie source + subtitle langs are configured in user_config_dir/yth/config.toml.
34	
35	Mirrors the structure of `mlf` (see dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_mlf) and pairs
36	with the `tv yth` channel (dot_config/television/cable/yth.toml).
37	"""
38	from __future__ import annotations
39	
40	import os
41	import shutil
42	import subprocess
43	import sys
44	from pathlib import Path
45	
46	USAGE = """\
47	Usage: yth [<subcommand>] [args...]
48	
49	Bare `yth` opens the `tv yth` fuzzy picker. Subcommands bypass it.
50	
51	  import-takeout <file>              Import a Google Takeout watch-history.json.
52	  sync                               Incremental :ythistory sync (needs cookies).
53	  enrich [--limit N | --all]         Fetch per-video metadata (public: no cookies).
54	  fetch-subs <id>... | --recent N    Download + index subtitle text.
55	             | --all
56	  search <query> [--subs] [--json]   FTS5 search (title/channel/description;
57	         [--limit N] [--raw]         --subs also matches captions).
58	  list [--tsv] [--limit N]           List history, newest first (--tsv for tv).
59	  show <id> [--json]                 One-video detail (DB-only).
60	  open <id> | copy <id> | play <id>  Open / copy URL / play.
61	
62	Examples:
63	  yth import-takeout ~/Downloads/watch-history.json
64	  yth search "rust async" --subs
65	  yth enrich --limit 200
66	  yth fetch-subs --recent 50
67	  yth show dQw4w9WgXcQ
68	"""
69	
70	
71	def _source_path() -> Path:
72	    """Locate the chezmoi source dir so we can import scripts.yth.*.
73	
74	    Identical strategy to executable_mlf:_source_path / executable_fleet.
75	    Trust `chezmoi source-path`; fall back to ~/.local/share/chezmoi.
76	    """
77	    chezmoi = shutil.which("chezmoi")
78	    if chezmoi:
79	        try:
80	            out = subprocess.run(
81	                [chezmoi, "source-path"],
82	                capture_output=True, text=True, check=False, timeout=5,
83	            )
84	            if out.returncode == 0 and out.stdout.strip():
85	                return Path(out.stdout.strip())
86	        except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError):
87	            pass
88	    fallback = Path.home() / ".local" / "share" / "chezmoi"
89	    if (fallback / "scripts" / "yth" / "__init__.py").is_file():
90	        return fallback
91	    print(
92	        "yth: cannot locate chezmoi source dir.\n"
93	        "  Tried: `chezmoi source-path` and ~/.local/share/chezmoi.\n"
94	        "  Install chezmoi or ensure the source dir exists.",
95	        file=sys.stderr,
96	    )
97	    sys.exit(2)
98	
99	
100	def _dispatch_tv(args: list[str]) -> int:
101	    """Exec `tv yth` (the picker). Replaces this process so Ctrl+C reaches tv."""
102	    tv = shutil.which("tv")
103	    if not tv:
104	        print(
105	            "yth: `tv` (television) not in PATH — run a subcommand instead,\n"
106	            "  e.g. `yth search <query>` or `yth list`.  `yth -h` for help.",
107	            file=sys.stderr,
108	        )
109	        return 2
110	    os.execvp(tv, [tv, "yth", *args])
111	
112	
113	def _leaf(module: str, prog: str, args: list[str]) -> int:
114	    """Rewrite argv and hand off to a leaf module's tyro-based main()."""
115	    sys.argv = [prog, *args]
116	    mod = __import__(f"scripts.yth.{module}", fromlist=["main"])
117	    return mod.main()
118	
119	
120	def _dispatch_open(args: list[str]) -> int:
121	    if not args or not args[0].strip():
122	        print("yth open: missing <id> argument", file=sys.stderr)
123	        return 2
124	    from scripts.yth import open_id
125	
126	    return open_id(args[0])
127	
128	
129	def _dispatch_copy(args: list[str]) -> int:
130	    if not args or not args[0].strip():
131	        print("yth copy: missing <id> argument", file=sys.stderr)
132	        return 2
133	    from scripts.yth import copy_id
134	
135	    return copy_id(args[0])
136	
137	
138	def _dispatch_play(args: list[str]) -> int:
139	    if not args or not args[0].strip():
140	        print("yth play: missing <id> argument", file=sys.stderr)
141	        return 2
142	    from scripts.yth import play_id
143	
144	    return play_id(args[0])
145	
146	
147	def main() -> int:
148	    # Help paths print USAGE and exit BEFORE any heavy import, so
149	    # `yth -h | grep ...` stays fast + scriptable and never loads yt_dlp.
150	    if len(sys.argv) >= 2 and sys.argv[1] in ("-h", "--help", "help"):
151	        print(USAGE)
152	        return 0
153	
154	    src = _source_path()
155	    if str(src) not in sys.path:
156	        sys.path.insert(0, str(src))
157	
158	    # Bare `yth` → tv picker.
159	    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
160	        return _dispatch_tv([])
161	
162	    sub = sys.argv[1]
163	    rest = sys.argv[2:]
164	
165	    # Leaf modules own their own tyro parsing. Subcommand `-` → module `_`.
166	    leaves = {
167	        "import-takeout": ("import_takeout", "yth import-takeout"),
168	        "sync": ("sync", "yth sync"),
169	        "enrich": ("enrich", "yth enrich"),
170	        "fetch-subs": ("fetch_subs", "yth fetch-subs"),
171	        "search": ("search", "yth search"),
172	        "list": ("list", "yth list"),
173	        "show": ("show", "yth show"),
174	    }
175	    if sub in leaves:
176	        module, prog = leaves[sub]
177	        return _leaf(module, prog, rest)
178	
179	    shims = {"open": _dispatch_open, "copy": _dispatch_copy, "play": _dispatch_play}
180	    if sub in shims:
181	        return shims[sub](rest)
182	    if sub == "tv":
183	        return _dispatch_tv(rest)
184	
185	    print(f"yth: unknown subcommand '{sub}'\n\n{USAGE}", file=sys.stderr)
186	    return 2
187	
188	
189	if __name__ == "__main__":
190	    sys.exit(main())
191

1	# 48_pqsum_completion.bash - tab completion for `pqsum` (pueue queue summary).
2	# Source CLI: dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_pqsum (argparse).
3	# Dynamic group completion via `pueue status --json | jq`.
4	
5	command -v pqsum >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
6	
7	_pqsum_completion() {
8	    local cur prev words cword
9	    _init_completion -n = || return
10	
11	    case "$prev" in
12	        -g|--group)
13	            if command -v pueue >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
14	                local groups
15	                groups=$(pueue status --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.groups | keys[]' 2>/dev/null)
16	                COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "$groups" -- "$cur") )
17	            fi
18	            return
19	            ;;
20	        --out)
21	            _filedir
22	            return
23	            ;;
24	        --host)
25	            return
26	            ;;
27	    esac
28	
29	    case "$cur" in
30	        -*)
31	            local opts="-h --help -g --group --report --out --clean --yes --multi-host --stdin-json --raw-stdin --host --deep -r --refresh --no-cache --dry-run"
32	            COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "$opts" -- "$cur") )
33	            ;;
34	        *)
35	            # Only one positional (mode) — count non-flag words so far.
36	            local i pos=0
37	            for ((i = 1; i < cword; i++)); do
38	                case "${words[i]}" in
39	                    -*) ;;
40	                    *) ((pos++)) ;;
41	                esac
42	            done
43	            if [ "$pos" -eq 0 ]; then
44	                COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "text ai json" -- "$cur") )
45	            fi
46	            ;;
47	    esac
48	}
49	
50	complete -F _pqsum_completion pqsum

604	| `logtail` | function | `dot_config/shell/29_log_tools.sh` | `tail -f` with live tailspin highlighting (prefers `tspin --follow`, falls back to `tail -F \| tspin --print`) |
605	| `svclog` | function | `dot_config/shell/29_log_tools.sh` | Cross-platform service log follower — `journalctl -fu` on Linux, `tail -F StdoutPath` / `log stream --predicate` on macOS, piped through tailspin. Accepts `--user` for user-scope. Usage: `svclog [--user] <service>`. See [services.md](../tools/services.md) |

Defaults are already vim-flavored (h/j/k/l, gg/G, /? search). Companion rc at `~/.visidatarc` (chezmoi-managed via [`dot_visidatarc.tmpl`](../../dot_visidatarc.tmpl)) carries the feather/StringDtype workaround and `enableVimMode`-gated key rebinds — see [vim-mode.md → VisiData](../this_repo/vim-mode.md#visidata).

Escape hatch for `.feather` / `.arrow` files where the default PandasSheet path crashes on pandas `StringDtype` columns (`ValueError: Could not convert ... to NumPy dtype`). Full diagnosis: [pitfalls/visidata-feather-stringdtype-numpy-dtype.md](../../pitfalls/visidata-feather-stringdtype-numpy-dtype.md) |
617	| `vd-ro` | alias | `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh` | `visidata --readonly` — open in read-only mode so a stray `g Ctrl+S` cannot overwrite the source. `--readonly` is an optalias for `--overwrite=n` (`visidata/modify.py:11`); in-memory edits are still allowed but the save path fails. Pair with `vd-arrow` (e.g. `visidata --readonly -f arrow file.feather`) when both protections are wanted. See [vim-mode.md → VisiData → Data safety](../this_repo/vim-mode.md#data-safety-read-only-mode) |

628	| `audit-failed-logins` | function | `dot_config/shell/45_audit.sh.tmpl` | Failed login attempts via `lastb -F -i` (Linux btmp). Requires sudo. |

```text
125	### D. No completion support
126	
127	`claude`, `gemini`, `agy`/`agyc` (Antigravity CLI), `btop`, `lazygit` -- no generation command available.
128	
129	### E. Python tools via `shtab` / `tyro` / `click` / `argcomplete`
130	
131	Python CLI frameworks can generate completions. Pick by what your script uses:
132	
133	- **[tyro](https://brentyi.github.io/tyro/tab_completion/)** (this repo's `mi-router` + every `scripts/fleet/*.py` and `scripts/mlf/*.py` subcommand): `<tool> --tyro-write-completion zsh <path>`. Native flag — auto-added when you call `tyro.cli(...)`. tyro emits `#compdef <full-binary-path>` for zsh, so post-process the first line to the short name (see `dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh` for the canonical pattern). Bash output already binds `basename`, no fixup needed.
134	- **[shtab](https://github.com/iterative/shtab)**: `shtab --shell=zsh my_module.parser > ~/.zfunc/_my_tool`. Decorate-an-`argparse.ArgumentParser` style; works for both shells.
135	- **argcomplete**: `register-python-argcomplete tool_name` (eval-at-startup style, category C). Requires the script to call `argcomplete.autocomplete(parser)` before `parse_args()`. Cross-shell.
136	- **click** (used by `marimo`, `thefuck`, `mlflow`, `litellm`, etc.): `_TOOL_COMPLETE=zsh_source tool > ~/.zfunc/_tool`. The completion script may include side effects (aliases / functions) — if so, treat as category C and cache via `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/<shell>/<tool>_completion.<ext>`. See the canonical pattern at `dot_config/shell/29_marimo.sh`.
137	
138	> **TAB display itself**, not just completion data: see [`oh-my-zsh-plugins.md`](oh-my-zsh-plugins.md) "TAB display upgrades — alternatives evaluated" for fzf-tab (recommended) and rejected alternatives (zsh-autocomplete / carapace-bin / inshellisense).
139	
140	### F. In-house CLIs (this repo)
141	
142	| CLI | Source | Framework | Strategy | Files |
143	|---|---|---|---|---|
144	| `mi-router` | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_mi-router` | tyro | A (lazy autoload) | `dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh` (gen + mtime check); refresh helper `mi-router-update-completion` |
145	| `mi-dhcp-bind` | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_mi-dhcp-bind` | tyro | A (lazy autoload) | `dot_config/shell/46_mi_dhcp_bind.sh` (gen + mtime check); refresh helper `mi-dhcp-bind-update-completion` |
146	| `reyee` | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_reyee` | tyro | A (lazy autoload) | `dot_config/shell/48_reyee.sh` (gen + mtime check); refresh helper `reyee-update-completion` |
147	| `ping-monitor` | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_ping-monitor` | bash hand-rolled | B | `dot_config/zsh/tools/50_ping_monitor_completion.zsh` + `dot_config/bash/50_ping_monitor_completion.bash` |
148	| `fleet` | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_fleet` + `scripts/fleet/*.py` | hand-rolled umbrella + tyro/argparse subs | B (eager hand-written) | `dot_config/zsh/tools/45_fleet_completion.zsh` + `dot_config/bash/45_fleet_completion.bash` |
149	| `mlf` | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_mlf` + `scripts/mlf/*.py` | hand-rolled umbrella + tyro subs | B | `dot_config/zsh/tools/46_mlf_completion.zsh` + `dot_config/bash/46_mlf_completion.bash` |
150	| `pqsum` | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_pqsum` | argparse | B | `dot_config/zsh/tools/48_pqsum_completion.zsh` + `dot_config/bash/48_pqsum_completion.bash` |
151	| `x` | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x` | bash hand-rolled | B | `dot_config/zsh/tools/49_x_completion.zsh` + `dot_config/bash/49_x_completion.bash` |
152	| `dotcfg` | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_dotcfg` (thin shell → `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py reconfigure`) | bash wrapper | B | `dot_config/zsh/tools/51_dotcfg_completion.zsh` + `dot_config/bash/51_dotcfg_completion.bash` (keys mirror PROMPTS) |
153	| `agent-warmup` | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_agent-warmup` | argparse (subcommands) | B | `dot_config/zsh/tools/52_agent_warmup_completion.zsh` + `dot_config/bash/52_agent_warmup_completion.bash` |
154	| `yth` | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_yth` + `scripts/yth/*.py` | hand-rolled umbrella + tyro subs | B | `dot_config/zsh/tools/53_yth_completion.zsh` + `dot_config/bash/53_yth_completion.bash` |
155	| `wake` | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_wake` | argparse | B | `dot_config/zsh/tools/54_wake_completion.zsh` + `dot_config/bash/54_wake_completion.bash` |
156	| `aiblock` | `scripts/aiblock.py` | questionary (interactive TUI) | — (no CLI args) | (not needed) |
157	
158	**Dynamic candidates wired up:**
159	
160	- `fleet` host names — `_fleet_hosts_one` / `_fleet_hosts_csv` shell out to `fleet hosts --list`. Used for the positional `fleet hosts NAME`, `fleet chezmoi diff HOST`, `fleet chezmoi tail HOST`, and the `--hosts=foo,bar,baz` CSV flag everywhere.
161	- `pqsum -g <GROUP>` — `_pqsum` shells out to `pueue status --json | jq '.groups | keys[]'`.
162	- `mlf` ids (run-id, experiment-id, model-name) — **not** auto-completed (would round-trip MLflow tracking server, possibly auth-required). Use `tv mlflow` for fuzzy id picking instead.
163	- `yth` video ids — **not** auto-completed (opaque 11-char ids; enumerating the whole history on every TAB is wasteful). Use `tv yth` or `yth search <query>` instead.
164	- `wake` host names — `_wake` shells out to `wake --list-names` (reads `~/.config/wake/hosts.toml`), same pattern as `_fleet_hosts_one`.
165	
166	**Adding a new in-house CLI** (decision flow):
167	
168	1. **Does it use tyro?** → Use Strategy A. Mirror `dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh`. Add a `<tool>-update-completion` helper to `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh`. Don't forget to rewrite `#compdef` in zsh post-gen.
169	2. **Does it use argparse?** → Two sub-options:
170	   - Add `argcomplete.autocomplete(parser)` to the script + Strategy C cached eval at startup.
171	   - Hand-write Strategy B completion (smaller / no Python dependency at every shell startup).
172	3. **Hand-rolled / shell script** → Strategy B hand-written. One zsh file in `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<name>_completion.zsh`, one bash file in `dot_config/bash/<NN>_<name>_completion.bash`. Mirror `_fleet`'s structure: top-level dispatcher → per-subcommand functions → dynamic helpers.
173	4. **Update this table + `docs/shells/aliases.md`** in the same commit (per the cross-file maintenance rule in `CLAUDE.md`).
174	
175	## Why `~/.zfunc/` is NOT Tracked by Chezmoi
176	
177	**Decision: `~/.zfunc/` is not version-controlled.** Rationale:
178	
179	1. **Completions are tool-version-dependent.** A completion script generated by `uv 0.6` may not match `uv 0.7`. Tracking stale files causes subtle breakage.
180	2. **Not all users install the same tools.** A `_pueue` completion file is useless (and throws warnings) if pueue isn't installed.
181	3. **Regeneration is trivial.** One command per tool.
182	4. **Brew-installed tools auto-manage their completions** via site-functions. Duplicating them in `~/.zfunc/` creates conflicts.
183	
184	### What we DO track
185	
186	- `fpath+=~/.zfunc` in `dot_zshrc.tmpl` (ensures the directory is in the search path)
187	- `zsh-completions` plugin cloned by ansible (community completions)
188	- `~/.docker/completions` fpath entry
189	- Tool-specific `eval`/`source` integrations in `dot_config/zsh/tools/`
190	
191	## Generating Completions After Fresh Install
192	
193	**Automatic — no manual step needed.** Every `chezmoi apply` runs `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_after_50_generate_completions.sh.tmpl`, which calls `scripts/generate_completions.sh` and regenerates completion for the 14 self-generating tools listed in Section A (`chezmoi`, `mise`, `uv`, `just`, `starship`, `gh`, `docker`, `rg`, `fd`, `bat`, `delta`, `zellij`, `pueue`, `opencode`).
194	
195	The hook is **idempotent** — it stat-checks each tool's binary mtime against the existing completion file and skips if the cache is fresh. Cost when nothing changed: **~21ms** total (presence checks + 28 stat calls). After an `ansible-playbook` / `brew upgrade` / `mise install <NEW>` that bumps a binary's mtime: ~140ms one-shot to regenerate the affected completions.
196	
197	Output paths:
198	- **zsh**: `~/.zfunc/_<tool>` — lazy-loaded by compinit on first TAB (in `$fpath` via `dot_zshrc.tmpl:68`).
199	- **bash**: `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/bash-completion/completions/<tool>` — lazy-loaded by bash-completion v2 on first TAB.
```
