---

## A) `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` (4426 lines)

### A1. Top-of-file "Tools:" comment (line 3)

This is the master tool list you'd append `doxx` to:

```yaml
# Line 3
# Tools: bat, bats, gh, glab, diffnav, gh-dash, gh-notify, eza, git-delta, git-graph, tldr, glow, gum, vhs, freeze, thefuck, zoxide, direnv, yazi, superfile, tmux, sesh, worktrunk, workmux, zellij, herdr, btop, htop, duckdb, rclone, coreutils, taplo, television, pandoc, tailspin, lnav, grc, ccze (Linux only), dasel, yq, jnv, witr, figlet, toilet, lolcat, fastfetch, mosh
```

### A2. macOS Homebrew tap pattern (workmux — your closest analog)

There are three moving parts on macOS for a tapped formula. **(a)** the `homebrew_tap` task (lines 15-23), **(b)** the tap must be added to the trust loop (lines 25-51), **(c)** the formula name added to the big `homebrew` install list (line 78).

**(a) Tap the formula** — lines 9-23 (diffnav shown for contrast, workmux is the tarball analog):

```yaml
- name: Tap diffnav formula (macOS)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  community.general.homebrew_tap:
    name: dlvhdr/formulae
    state: present

- name: Tap raine/workmux formula (macOS)
  # workmux is a tmux + git-worktree orchestrator with first-class agent
  # status icons (🤖 working / 💬 waiting / ✅ done) rendered into the tmux
  # window list. Coexists with worktrunk (`wt`); see docs/tools/workmux.md
  # for the wt-vs-wm split.
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  community.general.homebrew_tap:
    name: raine/workmux
    state: present
```

**(b) Trust the tap** (Homebrew 6.0 formula-trust gate) — lines 25-51. Note the comment at line 31 explicitly says to keep this loop in sync with the taps above:

```yaml
# Homebrew 6.0 added a formula-trust security gate: `brew install` refuses to
# load formulae from third-party taps until the tap is explicitly trusted
# ("Error: Refusing to load formula <tap>/<formula> from untrusted tap"). The
# homebrew_tap module has no trust parameter, so trust via `brew trust`.
# Idempotent + back-compatible: older Homebrew has no trust concept, so
# `tap-info` won't contain "Untrusted" and the trust task no-ops (no version
# gate needed). Keep this loop in sync with the third-party taps above — add any
# new third-party tap here too. See pitfalls/homebrew-6-refuses-untrusted-tap-formula.md
- name: Check trust state of third-party taps (macOS, Homebrew >= 6.0 formula-trust gate)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  ansible.builtin.command: "brew tap-info {{ item }}"
  loop:
    - dlvhdr/formulae
    - raine/workmux
  register: devtools_tap_info
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false

- name: Trust untrusted third-party taps (macOS)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
    - "'Untrusted' in item.stdout"
  ansible.builtin.command: "brew trust {{ item.item }}"
  loop: "{{ devtools_tap_info.results }}"
  loop_control:
    label: "{{ item.item }}"
  changed_when: true
```

Note for doxx: the tap is `bgreenwell/tap`, so you'd add `name: bgreenwell/tap` in a new `homebrew_tap` task and add `bgreenwell/tap` to the `loop:` list at lines 36-38.

### A4. Linux GitHub-release-tarball download+extract pattern (workmux — full block, lines 3242-3383)

This is the exact `.tar.gz` pattern to copy for doxx on Linux. Structure: `command --version` idempotency check → `block:` guarded by `rc != 0` and architecture → mkdir `~/.local/bin` → `uri` GitHub API latest release → arch mapping `set_fact` → build download URL by `selectattr` on asset name → `get_url` to `/tmp` → mkdir temp → `ansible.builtin.unarchive` → `find` binary → `fail` if not found → `copy` to `~/.local/bin` → cleanup, all wrapped in `rescue:`.

```yaml
# --- workmux (tmux + git-worktree orchestrator with agent status icons) ---
# Coexists with worktrunk (`wt`); see docs/tools/workmux.md.
# Releases ship plain `.tar.gz` (NOT `.tar.xz` like worktrunk), so no xz dep.
- name: Check if workmux is installed
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
  ansible.builtin.command: wm --version
  register: workmux_check
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false
  environment:
    PATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"

- name: Install workmux from GitHub releases (Debian/Ubuntu, user-level)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - workmux_check.rc != 0
    - target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64', 'aarch64', 'arm64']
  block:
    - name: Ensure ~/.local/bin exists (workmux)
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
        state: directory
        mode: '0755'

    - name: Get latest workmux release
      ansible.builtin.uri:
        url: https://api.github.com/repos/raine/workmux/releases/latest
        return_content: true
      register: workmux_release

    - name: Set workmux architecture mapping
      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
        workmux_arch: >-
          {{
            'amd64' if target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
            else 'arm64' if target_architecture in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
            else ''
          }}

    - name: Skip workmux on unsupported architecture
      when: workmux_arch | trim == ''
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: "workmux skipped: no release for {{ target_architecture }}"

    - name: Set workmux download URL fact
      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
        workmux_download_url: >-
          {{
            (
              workmux_release.json.assets
              | selectattr('name', 'equalto', 'workmux-linux-' ~ workmux_arch ~ '.tar.gz')
              | map(attribute='browser_download_url')
              | first
            )
            | default('', true)
          }}

    - name: Skip workmux if download URL could not be determined
      when: workmux_download_url | trim == ''
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: "workmux skipped: could not determine download URL for architecture {{ workmux_arch }}"

    - name: Download workmux tarball
      when: workmux_download_url | trim != ''
      ansible.builtin.get_url:
        url: "{{ workmux_download_url }}"
        dest: /tmp/workmux.tar.gz
        mode: '0644'
        timeout: 120
      retries: 3
      delay: 5

    - name: Create workmux temp directory
      when: workmux_download_url | trim != ''
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: /tmp/workmux
        state: directory
        mode: '0755'

    - name: Extract workmux
      when: workmux_download_url | trim != ''
      ansible.builtin.unarchive:
        src: /tmp/workmux.tar.gz
        dest: /tmp/workmux
        remote_src: true

    - name: Find workmux binary
      when: workmux_download_url | trim != ''
      ansible.builtin.find:
        paths: /tmp/workmux
        patterns: workmux
        file_type: file
        recurse: true
      register: workmux_find

    - name: Fail if workmux binary was not found in extracted archive
      when:
        - workmux_download_url | trim != ''
        - workmux_find.matched | default(0) | int == 0
      ansible.builtin.fail:
        msg: "workmux binary not found under /tmp/workmux after extraction"

    - name: Install workmux to ~/.local/bin
      when:
        - workmux_download_url | trim != ''
        - workmux_find.matched | default(0) | int > 0
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        src: "{{ workmux_find.files[0].path }}"
        dest: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/workmux"
        mode: '0755'
        remote_src: true

    - name: Symlink wm -> workmux for short alias
      when:
        - workmux_download_url | trim != ''
        - workmux_find.matched | default(0) | int > 0
      ansible.builtin.file:
        src: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/workmux"
        dest: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/wm"
        state: link
        force: true

    - name: Clean up workmux temp files
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ item }}"
        state: absent
      loop:
        - /tmp/workmux.tar.gz
        - /tmp/workmux

  rescue:
    - name: Warn workmux installation failed
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: "workmux installation failed (likely network timeout) - skipping"

    - name: Clean up workmux temp files after failure
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ item }}"
        state: absent
      loop:
        - /tmp/workmux.tar.gz
        - /tmp/workmux
```

### A5. Idempotency / `creates:` guards, and unarchive-vs-unzip

**Idempotency guard style (devtools uses `command --version` + `rc != 0`, NOT `creates:`):** Linux tool tasks register a `<tool>_check` from `<tool> --version` with `changed_when: false` / `failed_when: false`, then gate the install `block:` on `<tool>_check.rc != 0` (workmux lines 3245-3257; herdr lines 4294-4306). The `--version` probe runs with an `environment: PATH` that prepends `~/.local/bin` so a prior user-level install is seen.

**`.tar.gz` → `ansible.builtin.unarchive` (confirmed):** The workmux Linux extract (lines 3321-3326) uses `ansible.builtin.unarchive` with `remote_src: true`. This is safe re: the BSD-tar pitfall because the whole block is guarded `when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"` (line 3246/3256) — it only ever runs on Linux (GNU tar). The macOS side never extracts a tarball; it goes through Homebrew. This matches your memory note. The herdr comment at line 4291 explicitly states the single-binary path "sidesteps the macOS BSD-tar .tar.gz pitfall entirely" — reinforcing that `.tar.gz` extraction is deliberately Linux-only here.

**`.zip` → NOT `ansible.builtin.unzip`; they shell out to Python's zipfile.** For zip assets (duckdb, rclone, yazi, lnav) the repo avoids a system `unzip` dependency by running `python3 -m zipfile -e <file.zip> <dest>` via `ansible.builtin.shell` (e.g. rclone line 2061, yazi line 2306, lnav line 3664). Relevant since doxx Linux ships `.tar.gz`, so you want the `unarchive` path (workmux), not these. There is also a `.gz` single-file case (taplo) that uses `gunzip -f` at line 3435.

**Single static binary (no archive) alternative — herdr, lines 4287-4370:** If doxx's Linux release were a bare binary you'd copy this, but doxx ships a tarball, so workmux is the right template. Included for completeness — herdr does `get_url` straight to `~/.local/bin/herdr` with `mode: '0755'` (lines 4357-4365), no unarchive.

Note on doxx Linux asset naming: your tarball is `doxx-$(uname -s)-$(uname -m).tar.gz` → on Linux that resolves to `doxx-Linux-x86_64.tar.gz` / `doxx-Linux-aarch64.tar.gz` (capital "Linux", raw `uname -m` arch). So in the `selectattr('name', 'equalto', ...)` you'd map arch to `x86_64`/`aarch64` (like herdr's mapping at lines 4315-4322, which keeps `x86_64`/`aarch64`), not to `amd64`/`arm64` (workmux's mapping). The workmux block gives the tarball extract mechanics; the herdr block gives the correct `x86_64`/`aarch64` arch mapping — you'd combine them.

## B) `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml` (105 lines)

### B1. Top-of-file comment — schema doc, NOT a tool list

Lines 1-28 are a detailed **schema** comment (documenting each per-entry key), not a flat "Tools:" list like devtools has. There is no separate one-line tool inventory to update here; you just append an entry to the `python_uv_tools:` list. The schema comment:

```yaml
---
# Python CLI tools installed via uv tool install
# Each tool has:
#   - name: package name (can include extras like [cli])
#   - binary: executable name to check for idempotency
#   - with: (optional) additional dependency to install with --with
#   - with_executables_from: (optional) list of packages to install AND
#     expose their entry points in ~/.local/bin (e.g. jupyter-core to get
#     the `jupyter` meta-CLI; `notebook` to get `jupyter-notebook`)
#     NOTE: requires uv >= 0.8.5 (--with-executables-from added in that release)
#     For the meta-CLI dispatch model + the 8 jupyter binaries this exposes,
#     see docs/tools/notebooks.md "The `jupyter` meta-CLI vs standalone binaries".
#     For the auto-upgrade dispatch when uv is too old, see docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md.
#   - extra_binaries: (optional) list of additional binary names that must
#     also exist in ~/.local/bin for the install to be considered complete.
#     Use this whenever `with_executables_from` is set, so adding a new
#     entry-point package later triggers a `--force` reinstall on machines
#     that already have `binary` present from a prior apply. Without this,
#     ansible's `creates:` guard short-circuits the install command and the
#     new exec shims are never written. See
#     pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md.
#   - python: (optional) pin Python version (e.g. "3.11" for thefuck)
#   - needs_modern_gcc: (optional, default false) tool transitively pulls
#     numpy 2.x / pandas 3.x / pyarrow which require GCC ≥ 9.3 to compile
#     from source. Skipped on systems where GCC < 9 (e.g. CentOS 7's
#     gcc 4.8.5). uv falls back to source build because numpy 2.x
#     dropped manylinux_2_17 wheels — see
#     pitfalls/centos7-numpy-pandas-source-build.md.
```

### B2. The `visidata` entry + neighbors (schema examples)

`visidata` — lines 54-64. Note `binary:` differs from `name:` (`vd` vs `visidata`), plus `needs_modern_gcc` and `with:`:

```yaml
  - name: visidata
    binary: vd
    needs_modern_gcc: true  # explicit pandas + pyarrow deps
    with:
      - pandas
      - pyarrow  # Required for parquet/feather/arrow loaders. Note: .feather
                 # files whose schema metadata marks columns as pandas
                 # StringDtype still crash the default PandasSheet path even
                 # with pyarrow installed; the dot_visidatarc override
                 # routes .feather → ArrowSheet to dodge that. See
                 # pitfalls/visidata-feather-stringdtype-numpy-dtype.md.

Simplest possible entries (this is what a plain `markitdown` would look like — `name` == package, `binary` == executable, nothing else) — lines 31-53:

```yaml
python_uv_tools:
  - name: thefuck
    binary: thefuck
    python: "3.11"  # Python 3.13 removed distutils which thefuck still uses
  - name: apprise

  - name: sqlit-tui[ssh]

## C) `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/tasks/main.yml` (248 lines) — how entries are consumed

The install loop is a single `ansible.builtin.command` templating `uv tool install` flags, looping over `python_uv_tools`. There is no `creates:`; idempotency is done via a pre-probe `stat` of extra_binaries plus a `_primary_exists` path check, combined in `when:` / `changed_when:`.

**Pre-probe of extra_binaries** — lines 193-202:

```yaml
- name: Probe extra_binaries presence (for entries using with_executables_from)
  ansible.builtin.stat:
    path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/{{ item.1 }}"
  loop: >-
    {{ python_uv_tools
       | subelements('extra_binaries', skip_missing=True) }}
  loop_control:
    label: "{{ item.0.name }} -> {{ item.1 }}"
  register: _uv_extra_binaries_probe
  changed_when: false
```

**The install task** — lines 204-249. Note the flag templating (lines 205-211): `--force` when extras missing, then `{{ item.name }}`, then optional `--python`, `--with`, and `--with-executables-from` loops. The idempotency logic lives in `vars:` (`_missing_extras`, `_force_reinstall`, `_primary_exists`), `changed_when:` (line 236), and `when:` (lines 240-242):

```yaml
- name: Install Python CLI tools via uv
  ansible.builtin.command: >-
    uv tool install
    {% if _force_reinstall %}--force {% endif %}
    {{ item.name }}
    {% if item.python is defined %}--python {{ item.python }} {% endif %}
    {% if item.with is defined %}{% for dep in item.with %}--with {{ dep }} {% endfor %}{% endif %}
    {% if item.with_executables_from is defined %}{% for dep in item.with_executables_from %}--with-executables-from {{ dep }} {% endfor %}{% endif %}
  vars:
    # True when ANY declared extra_binary is missing on disk. We can't use
    # `creates:` for these entries because the primary `binary` may already
    # exist from a previous apply (before `with_executables_from` was added
    # or extended), causing ansible to skip the command and never write the
    # new shims. See pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md.
    _extras: "{{ item.extra_binaries | default([]) }}"
    _missing_extras: >-
      {{ _uv_extra_binaries_probe.results
         | default([])
         | selectattr('item.0.name', 'equalto', item.name)
         | rejectattr('stat.exists')
         | map(attribute='item.1')
         | list }}
    _force_reinstall: "{{ _missing_extras | length > 0 }}"
    _primary_binary_path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/{{ item.binary }}"
    _primary_exists: "{{ _primary_binary_path is exists }}"
  register: python_uv_tool_install
  until: python_uv_tool_install is succeeded
  retries: 3
  delay: 5
  # Skip when:
  #   - primary binary already exists, AND
  #   - either no extras declared, or all extras already present
  changed_when: python_uv_tool_install.rc == 0 and (_force_reinstall or not _primary_exists)
  environment:
    UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT: "120"
    UV_HTTP_RETRIES: "5"
  when:
    - not (item.needs_modern_gcc | default(false) and gcc_too_old)
    - (not _primary_exists) or _force_reinstall
  loop: "{{ python_uv_tools }}"
  loop_control:
    label: >-
      {{ item.name
         }}{% if item.needs_modern_gcc | default(false) and gcc_too_old %} [SKIPPED: needs gcc >= 9]{% endif
         %}{% if item.extra_binaries is defined %} [extras: {{ item.extra_binaries | join(',') }}]{% endif %}
```

**How the pieces map for a simple entry (markitdown):** `binary:` drives `_primary_exists` (checks `~/.local/bin/markitdown` at line 227-228); with no `extra_binaries`, `_missing_extras` is empty → `_force_reinstall` is false → the install runs only when the binary is absent (`when:` line 242) and is marked changed only on first install (`changed_when:` line 236). The `extra_binaries` shim/`--force` machinery (lines 193-226) is entirely inert for entries without `with_executables_from`. There is also a GCC gate (`needs_modern_gcc`) at lines 174-191 and a uv-version gate at lines 29-164 — both irrelevant to a pure-Python single-entry tool like markitdown.

### B2. Best template for a Python self-bootstrapping uv tool

Two are directly relevant. **`executable_pqsum` is the best single-file argparse template** (self-contained, PEP723, argparse dispatch). **`executable_yth` is the best umbrella-dispatcher template** (thin launcher that imports `scripts/<name>/*` leaf modules and execs other tools). Both share the identical self-boot header.

**Self-boot shebang + PEP723 header (identical in `executable_pqsum`, `executable_yth`, `executable_mlf`):**
```python
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --quiet --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = [
#   "rich>=13.9",
# ]
# ///
```
`executable_yth` header (shows a richer dependency block):
```python
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --quiet --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = [
#   "yt-dlp>=2025.1",
#   "tyro>=0.9",
#   "rich>=13.9",
#   "platformdirs>=4",
# ]
# ///
```
The shebang `#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --quiet --script` is the self-bootstrap mechanism — uv reads the inline `# /// script` metadata, builds an ephemeral venv with those deps, and runs the file. No separate install step. (chezmoi's `executable_` prefix makes the deployed file `+x`.)

**Argument parsing / dispatch — `executable_pqsum` uses `argparse`** (imported at line 45). `executable_yth` hand-rolls a positional dispatcher (no argparse at the umbrella level; each leaf module owns its own `tyro` parsing). Neither uses click. The two dispatch styles:

`executable_yth` (umbrella → leaf-module dispatch), lines 147-190:
```python
def main() -> int:
    # Help paths print USAGE and exit BEFORE any heavy import
    if len(sys.argv) >= 2 and sys.argv[1] in ("-h", "--help", "help"):
        print(USAGE)
        return 0

    src = _source_path()
    if str(src) not in sys.path:
        sys.path.insert(0, str(src))

    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        return _dispatch_tv([])          # bare `yth` → tv picker

    sub = sys.argv[1]
    rest = sys.argv[2:]

    leaves = {
        "import-takeout": ("import_takeout", "yth import-takeout"),
        "sync": ("sync", "yth sync"),
        "search": ("search", "yth search"),
        "list": ("list", "yth list"),
        "show": ("show", "yth show"),
    }
    if sub in leaves:
        module, prog = leaves[sub]
        return _leaf(module, prog, rest)

    shims = {"open": _dispatch_open, "copy": _dispatch_copy, "play": _dispatch_play}
    if sub in shims:
        return shims[sub](rest)
    if sub == "tv":
        return _dispatch_tv(rest)

    print(f"yth: unknown subcommand '{sub}'\n\n{USAGE}", file=sys.stderr)
    return 2

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```
The leaf-handoff helper (rewrites argv, imports the module, calls its tyro `main()`), lines 113-117:
```python
def _leaf(module: str, prog: str, args: list[str]) -> int:
    sys.argv = [prog, *args]
    mod = __import__(f"scripts.yth.{module}", fromlist=["main"])
    return mod.main()
```

### B3. How the wrapper finds/execs other tools and handles PATH

**Two idioms in `executable_yth`:**

1. **Locate the chezmoi source dir** so leaf modules under `scripts/<name>/` are importable (lines 71-97):
```python
def _source_path() -> Path:
    chezmoi = shutil.which("chezmoi")
    if chezmoi:
        try:
            out = subprocess.run(
                [chezmoi, "source-path"],
                capture_output=True, text=True, check=False, timeout=5,
            )
            if out.returncode == 0 and out.stdout.strip():
                return Path(out.stdout.strip())
        except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError):
            pass
    fallback = Path.home() / ".local" / "share" / "chezmoi"
    if (fallback / "scripts" / "yth" / "__init__.py").is_file():
        return fallback
    print("yth: cannot locate chezmoi source dir. ...", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(2)
```
This is called out in yth's docstring as "Identical strategy to `executable_mlf:_source_path` / `executable_fleet`."

2. **Find + exec another tool via `shutil.which` + `os.execvp`** (replaces the process so signals propagate), lines 100-110:
```python
def _dispatch_tv(args: list[str]) -> int:
    tv = shutil.which("tv")
    if not tv:
        print("yth: `tv` (television) not in PATH — ...", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    os.execvp(tv, [tv, "yth", *args])
```

**`executable_pqsum`** finds AI CLIs by bare name in `subprocess`/`shutil.which` calls; its `AGENT_CONFIG` dict (lines 123-129) maps agent → argv-prefix (`["opencode","run",...]`, `["claude","-p",...]`, etc.), relying on inherited PATH. Neither launcher hard-codes PATH augmentation — that PATH-prelude pattern lives only in `scripts/fleet/pueue.py:_REMOTE_CMD` / `scripts/fleet/exec.py:_PATH_PRELUDE` (per CLAUDE.md), which is for *remote/cron* contexts, not local launchers. For a local `view-office` wrapper, the yth `shutil.which` + `os.execvp` pattern is the one to copy.

Note `executable_pqsum` also demonstrates the shared-SSOT loader pattern (lines 72-96) reading `~/.config/shell/04_ai_agents.sh` — only relevant if your tool needs AI config; a plain office viewer does not.

## C) COMPLETIONS

### C1. The two-file hand-written pattern (Strategy B eager-load)

Completions live in two separate directories, one file per shell, **eager-sourced** at shell startup (not lazy `~/.zfunc` autoload). Both guard on the command existing, then register.

**zsh file** — `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/zsh/tools/48_pqsum_completion.zsh` (verbatim):
```zsh
# 48_pqsum_completion.zsh - tab completion for `pqsum` (pueue queue summary).
(( $+commands[pqsum] )) || return 0

_pqsum() {
    local context state state_descr line
    typeset -A opt_args

    _arguments -C \
        '(- *)'{-h,--help}'[show help]' \
        '(-g --group)'{-g,--group}'=[restrict to one pueue group]:group:->group' \
        '--report[emit markdown report (ai mode only)]' \
        '--out=[write report to PATH]:path:_files' \
        ...
        '1:mode:(text ai json)'

    case "$state" in
        group)
            local -a groups
            if (( $+commands[pueue] )) && (( $+commands[jq] )); then
                groups=( ${(f)"$(pueue status --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.groups | keys[]' 2>/dev/null)"} )
                (( ${#groups} )) && _describe 'pueue group' groups
            fi
            ;;
    esac
}

compdef _pqsum pqsum
```

**bash file** — `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/bash/48_pqsum_completion.bash` (verbatim):
```bash
# 48_pqsum_completion.bash - tab completion for `pqsum` (pueue queue summary).
command -v pqsum >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0

_pqsum_completion() {
    local cur prev words cword
    _init_completion -n = || return

    case "$prev" in
        -g|--group)
            if command -v pueue >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                local groups
                groups=$(pueue status --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.groups | keys[]' 2>/dev/null)
                COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "$groups" -- "$cur") )
            fi
            return ;;
        --out) _filedir; return ;;
    esac

    case "$cur" in
        -*)
            local opts="-h --help -g --group --report --out --clean ..."
            COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "$opts" -- "$cur") ) ;;
        *)
            # positional (mode) counting ...
            COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "text ai json" -- "$cur") ) ;;
    esac
}

complete -F _pqsum_completion pqsum
```

 `https://yazi-rs.github.io/docs/cli/`

```text
Summary (from the doc page)

- Command to add a plugin (example):
  "ya pkg add yazi-rs/plugins:piper"

- Other useful exact commands:
  "ya pkg add owner/my-plugin"
  "ya pkg add yazi-rs/plugins:git"
  "ya pkg delete yazi-rs/plugins:git"
  "ya pkg list"
  "ya pkg install"
  "ya pkg upgrade"

How it works (paraphrased)
- When you add a package, ya will clone it from GitHub, copy it into your plugins directory, and update package.toml to lock its version (rev/hash).
- package.toml is the lockfile that ya updates and reads.
- "ya pkg install" installs all plugins with locked versions from package.toml on a new system.
- "ya pkg upgrade" upgrades all plugins to the latest versions.
- The command is "ya pkg" (current), not an older "ya pack".

Files & locations (quoted where exact)
- Package lockfile: "~/.config/yazi/package.toml"
- Plugins directory: "~/.config/yazi/plugins/"

package.toml format (example from the page; quoted lines kept short)
"[[plugin.deps]]use  = \"owner/my-plugin\""
"rev  = \"0573024\""
"hash = \"d81b64a39432fcd6224cd75d296e7510\""

"[[plugin.deps]]use  = \"yazi-rs/plugins:git\""
"rev  = \"9a1129c\""
"hash = \"a8e15d3c21c02a5af41d46ed04778a02\""

Notes
- You can pin a plugin by prefixing rev with "=" (example shown on the page).
- add/delete accept multiple packages at once (e.g. multiple args).
```
</details></tool-use>

<summary>Tool use: **WebFetch**</summary>
 `https://github.com/yazi-rs/plugins/tree/main/piper.yazi`

```text
What it is
- The plugin lets you run a shell command whose output becomes the preview. As the README puts it: "Pipe any shell command as a previewer."

Installation
- Install with ya: ya pkg add yazi-rs/plugins:piper

Configuration (prepend_previewers)
- piper is invoked with run = "piper -- <shell command>".
- The shell command can see these variables: "$1", "$w", "$h", "$t" (file path, preview width, height, theme). The README lists them as: "$1", "$w", "$h", "$t".

Exact yazi.toml example (prepend_previewers)
- Example setting piper as previewer for all URLs and passing the file path as $1:

[[plugin.prepend_previewers]]
url = "*"
run = 'piper -- echo "$1"'

Full working example: preview CSV files with bat
- This uses bat to pretty-print CSVs and honors width/theme variables:

[[plugin.prepend_previewers]]
url = "*.csv"
run = 'piper -- bat -p --color=always "$1"'

Alternate example: set theme based on $t

[[plugin.prepend_previewers]]
url = "*.csv"
run = 'piper -- bat -p --color=always --theme="$( [ "$t" = "dark" ] && echo Dracula || echo GitHub)" "$1"'

Notes
- Use the pipe form: run = "piper -- <your command>".
- The plugin repo used with ya is yazi-rs/plugins:piper.
```
</details></tool-use>

# Plan: Terminal Office-document viewing (doxx + markitdown + LibreOffice + `view-office` + yazi preview)

## Context

There is currently **no way to view Microsoft Office documents from the terminal** in this repo. Research (see the SpecStory history for this session) found the best-practice landscape is *per-format + two-mode* (quick glance vs. interactive read); no single tool covers everything. This machine already has `pandoc`, `visidata` (`vd`), `glow`, `bat`, `yazi`, `tv`, but is missing a real terminal-native Word viewer, an Office→markdown converter, and any integration wiring.

**Goal:** add the missing tools and a single dispatcher CLI so that (a) `view-office FILE` opens the right interactive viewer per extension, (b) `view-office --preview` emits ANSI/markdown to stdout, and (c) yazi previews Office files inline by calling that same dispatcher. Legacy binary formats (`.doc/.xls/.ppt`) are covered via LibreOffice headless conversion.

**User-confirmed choices** (this session):
1. Yazi previewer → **introduce the `ya pkg` plugin manager** (install `piper.yazi` properly; enables future plugins). This is the repo's first yazi-plugin mechanism.
2. Legacy formats → **add LibreOffice** (`soffice --headless --convert-to`) as a fallback dependency.
3. `view-office` scope → **smart dispatcher + `--preview` mode** (single source of truth that yazi/tv/fzf all call).

**Verified facts** (web + exploration): `doxx FILE` = interactive TUI; `doxx FILE --export ansi|markdown|text` (+ `-w COLS`) = stdout. `ya pkg add yazi-rs/plugins:piper` / `ya pkg install` / `ya pkg upgrade`; lockfile `~/.config/yazi/package.toml` (`[[plugin.deps]]` use/rev/hash); plugins land in `~/.config/yazi/plugins/`. piper previewer: `[[plugin.prepend_previewers]] url="*.docx" run='piper -- <cmd>'`, shell sees `$1` (path) `$w` (width) `$h` (height) `$t` (theme). markitdown = `uv tool install markitdown`, binary `markitdown`, converts docx/xlsx/**pptx**→markdown (pandoc canNOT read pptx/xlsx — do not use it for those).

---

Mirror the **workmux** treatment (tarball mechanics) but with **herdr's arch mapping** (asset is `doxx-Linux-<uname -m>.tar.gz` → `x86_64`/`aarch64`, not `amd64`/`arm64`).

No `wm`-style symlink needed.

### 2. Install `markitdown` (uv tool) — `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml`

- **Linux (Debian):** `ansible.builtin.apt` `name: libreoffice-nogui` (or `libreoffice` if `-nogui` unavailable) `state: present`, `become: true`, `tags: [sudo]` — mirror the pandoc apt task (~L2755). Add a comment noting it's a heavy (~hundreds of MB) fallback for legacy `.doc/.xls/.ppt` only.
- Append `libreoffice` to the L3 `# Tools:` comment.

### 4. `view-office` dispatcher CLI — `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_view-office`

**Language: POSIX/bash, NOT the Python uv-self-boot pattern.** Rationale: it sits on yazi's preview hot-path (invoked on every hover); `uv run --script` adds ~100-200ms startup, bash ~5ms. Deliberate divergence from `executable_pqsum`/`executable_yth` — document the reason in a header comment.

Interface: `view-office [--preview] [--width N] FILE`
- Resolve lowercase extension. `--width` defaults to `${COLUMNS:-100}`.
- Helper `have(){ command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }`; `soffice_bin()` = first of `soffice`/`libreoffice` on PATH, else macOS app path `/Applications/LibreOffice.app/Contents/MacOS/soffice`. Missing-tool → `view-office: <tool> not found — install via <role>` on stderr, exit 2.

| `.xlsx` | `vd "$f"` (visidata) | `markitdown "$f" \| glow -w "$width" -` |
| `.pptx` | `markitdown "$f" \| glow -p` | `markitdown "$f" \| glow -w "$width" -` |
| `.doc/.xls/.ppt/.odt/.ods/.odp/.rtf` | `soffice` convert → OOXML twin in `$(mktemp -d)` → **recurse** `view-office "$twin"` | same, with `--preview` |

Legacy conversion: `soffice --headless --convert-to <docx\|xlsx\|pptx> --outdir "$tmp" "$f"` then re-dispatch. Unknown ext → error + usage. `--help`/`-h` fast path prints usage.

- **New run-script** `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_46_yazi_plugins.sh.tmpl` (pick a free NN; 40=skills, 50=completions, so 46 is free). - `dot_config/bash/55_view_office_completion.bash` — mirror; `command -v view-office`; `_filedir`; header cross-refs the zsh twin + §F.

1	# 54_wake_completion.zsh - tab completion for `wake` (Wake-on-LAN sender).

3	# 54_wake_completion.bash — keep both in sync. See docs/zsh/zsh-completions.md §F.

6	# ~/.config/wake/hosts.toml), same pattern as `_fleet_hosts_one`.

15	        '--list-names[print bare host names]' \

18	        '(-c --count)'{-c,--count}'[packets per target]:count:' \
19	        '(-q --quiet)'{-q,--quiet}'[suppress per-packet output]' \
20	        '*:host or MAC:->targets'
21	    if [[ $state == targets ]]; then
22	        _describe -t hosts 'wake host' hosts
23	    fi
24	}

26	compdef _wake wake

1	# 54_wake_completion.bash - tab completion for `wake` (Wake-on-LAN sender).

7	_wake_completion() {
8	    local cur prev words cword
9	    _init_completion -n = || return
10	
11	    case "$prev" in
12	        -b|--broadcast|-p|--port|-c|--count) return ;;
13	    esac
14

16	        -*)
17	            COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "-l --list --list-names -b --broadcast -p --port -c --count -q --quiet" -- "$cur") )
18	            ;;

1	---
2	# Python CLI tools installed via uv tool install
3	# Each tool has:
4	#   - name: package name (can include extras like [cli])
5	#   - binary: executable name to check for idempotency
6	#   - with: (optional) additional dependency to install with --with
7	#   - with_executables_from: (optional) list of packages to install AND
8	#     expose their entry points in ~/.local/bin (e.g. jupyter-core to get
9	#     the `jupyter` meta-CLI; `notebook` to get `jupyter-notebook`)
10	#     NOTE: requires uv >= 0.8.5 (--with-executables-from added in that release)
11	#     For the meta-CLI dispatch model + the 8 jupyter binaries this exposes,
12	#     see docs/tools/notebooks.md "The `jupyter` meta-CLI vs standalone binaries".
13	#     For the auto-upgrade dispatch when uv is too old, see docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md.
14	#   - extra_binaries: (optional) list of additional binary names that must
15	#     also exist in ~/.local/bin for the install to be considered complete.
16	#     Use this whenever `with_executables_from` is set, so adding a new
17	#     entry-point package later triggers a `--force` reinstall on machines
18	#     that already have `binary` present from a prior apply. Without this,
19	#     ansible's `creates:` guard short-circuits the install command and the
20	#     new exec shims are never written. See
21	#     pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md.
22	#   - python: (optional) pin Python version (e.g. "3.11" for thefuck)
23	#   - needs_modern_gcc: (optional, default false) tool transitively pulls
24	#     numpy 2.x / pandas 3.x / pyarrow which require GCC ≥ 9.3 to compile
25	#     from source. Skipped on systems where GCC < 9 (e.g. CentOS 7's
26	#     gcc 4.8.5). uv falls back to source build because numpy 2.x
27	#     dropped manylinux_2_17 wheels — see
28	#     pitfalls/centos7-numpy-pandas-source-build.md.
29	
30	python_uv_tools:
31	  - name: thefuck
32	    binary: thefuck
33	    python: "3.11"  # Python 3.13 removed distutils which thefuck still uses
34	  - name: apprise

54	  - name: visidata
55	    binary: vd
56	    needs_modern_gcc: true  # explicit pandas + pyarrow deps
57	    with:

59	      - pyarrow  # Required for parquet/feather/arrow loaders. Note: .feather
60	                 # files whose schema metadata marks columns as pandas
61	                 # StringDtype still crash the default PandasSheet path even
62	                 # with pyarrow installed; the dot_visidatarc override
63	                 # routes .feather → ArrowSheet to dodge that. See

57	# OSC 52 clipboard copy: ships stdin bytes through a terminal escape sequence.
58	# Works over SSH with no X/Wayland as long as the terminal (or tmux with

60	# by an outer pipeline.

67	    [[ -n "$data" ]] || return 0

70	        # shellcheck disable=SC1003 # printf consumes the backslash escapes.
71	        printf '\033Ptmux;\033\033]52;c;%s\033\033\\\033\\' "$data" > /dev/tty
72	    else

74	        printf '\033]52;c;%s\033\\' "$data" > /dev/tty

191	copy_file_macos() {
192	    command -v osascript >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
193	
194	    # JXA + NSPasteboard.writeObjects, not AppleScript's `set the clipboard to
195	    # {POSIX file p}`: the latter only writes a legacy Apple Event 'furl'
196	    # descriptor. macOS advertises public.file-url/NSFilenamesPboardType as
197	    # available on it, but only old Carbon-coercion-aware readers (Finder,
198	    # AppleScript itself) can actually resolve that promise. Modern readers
199	    # (Raycast clipboard history, Chromium/Electron incl. Discord) call
200	    # NSPasteboardItem.string(forType:) directly and get nil. writeObjects
201	    # writes a real per-file public.file-url string up front, matching what
202	    # Finder's own Cmd+C produces.
203	    if osascript -l JavaScript - "$@" <<'JXA'
204	ObjC.import("AppKit");
205	function run(argv) {
206	    var pb = $.NSPasteboard.generalPasteboard;
207	    pb.clearContents;
208	    var urls = $.NSMutableArray.alloc.init;
209	    for (var i = 0; i < argv.length; i++) {
210	        urls.addObject($.NSURL.fileURLWithPath(argv[i]));
211	    }
212	    if (!pb.writeObjects(urls)) {
213	        throw new Error("writeObjects failed");
214	    }
215	}
216	JXA

219	    fi

222	    exit 1

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# view-office — open or preview Microsoft Office / OpenDocument files in the
# terminal. Dispatches by extension to the right tool:
#   .docx → doxx        .xlsx → visidata (vd)   .pptx → markitdown | glow
#   legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt/.odt/.ods/.odp/.rtf → LibreOffice headless converts to
#   the modern OOXML twin, then re-dispatches to the handler above.
#
# Two modes:
#   view-office FILE              interactive TUI / pager (default)
#   view-office --preview FILE    non-interactive ANSI/markdown to stdout
#
# Deliberately plain bash, NOT the `uv run --script` self-boot pattern used by
# executable_pqsum / yth / mlf: this sits on yazi's preview hot-path (invoked on
# every file hover via the piper.yazi previewer), where uv/Python startup
# (~100-200ms) would make previews feel laggy. Pure dispatch/exec is ~5ms.
#
# The yazi previewer contract (dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml) is:
#   run = 'piper -- view-office --preview --width "$w" "$1"'
# Keep --preview/--width in sync with that. See docs/tools/office-viewers.md.
set -euo pipefail

PREVIEW=0
WIDTH="${COLUMNS:-100}"

usage() {
    printf '%s\n' \
        "Usage: view-office [--preview] [--width N] FILE" \
        "" \
        "Open or preview an Office / OpenDocument file in the terminal." \
        "" \
        "Options:" \
        "  -p, --preview    Render to stdout (ANSI/markdown) instead of a TUI." \
        "  -w, --width N    Wrap width for --preview (default: \$COLUMNS or 100)." \
        "  -h, --help       Show this help." \
        "" \
        "Formats:" \
        "  .docx  doxx (interactive) / doxx --export ansi (preview)" \
        "  .xlsx  visidata vd (interactive) / markitdown | glow (preview)" \
        "  .pptx  markitdown | glow pager (interactive) / markitdown | glow (preview)" \
        "  .doc .xls .ppt .odt .ods .odp .rtf  LibreOffice → OOXML twin, then above"
}

err() { printf 'view-office: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

have() { command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }

# need TOOL "install hint" — fail with an actionable message if TOOL is absent.
need() {
    have "$1" && return 0
    err "$1 not found — $2"
    exit 2
}

# Resolve the LibreOffice headless binary: `soffice` / `libreoffice` on PATH,
# else the macOS .app bundle (the cask does not put soffice on PATH).
soffice_bin() {
    local b
    for b in soffice libreoffice; do
        if have "$b"; then printf '%s\n' "$b"; return 0; fi
    done
    if [[ -x /Applications/LibreOffice.app/Contents/MacOS/soffice ]]; then
        printf '%s\n' /Applications/LibreOffice.app/Contents/MacOS/soffice
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

# Render markdown from stdin: pretty ANSI via glow if present, else raw passthrough.
render_md() {
    if have glow; then
        glow -w "$WIDTH" -
    else
        cat
    fi
}

render_docx() {
    local f="$1"
    need doxx "install via the devtools ansible role (brew bgreenwell/tap/doxx)"
    if ((PREVIEW)); then
        doxx --export ansi -w "$WIDTH" "$f"
    else
        doxx "$f"
    fi
}

render_xlsx() {
    local f="$1"
    if ((PREVIEW)); then
        need markitdown "install via python_uv_tools (uv tool install markitdown)"
        markitdown "$f" | render_md
    else
        need vd "install visidata via python_uv_tools (uv tool install visidata)"
        vd "$f"
    fi
}

render_pptx() {
    local f="$1"
    need markitdown "install via python_uv_tools (uv tool install markitdown)"
    if ((PREVIEW)); then
        markitdown "$f" | render_md
    elif have glow; then
        markitdown "$f" | glow -p -
    else
        markitdown "$f" | "${PAGER:-less}"
    fi
}

# Legacy binary / OpenDocument formats: convert to the modern OOXML twin with
# LibreOffice headless (isolated -env profile so a running GUI instance doesn't
# lock us out), then re-dispatch. NOTE: we run the viewer as a child (no exec)
# so the EXIT trap still fires and cleans the tmpdir after an interactive TUI.
render_legacy() {
    local f="$1" target="$2" so tmp stem twin
    so="$(soffice_bin)" || {
        err "LibreOffice (soffice) not found — install via the devtools role (brew --cask libreoffice / apt libreoffice)"
        exit 2
    }
    tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
    trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
    if ! "$so" --headless -env:UserInstallation="file://$tmp/profile" \
            --convert-to "$target" --outdir "$tmp" "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        err "LibreOffice failed to convert $f → $target"
        exit 1
    fi
    stem="$(basename -- "$f")"; stem="${stem%.*}"
    twin="$tmp/$stem.$target"
    [[ -f "$twin" ]] || { err "converted file not found: $twin"; exit 1; }
    render "$twin"
}

render() {
    local f="$1" ext
    ext="${f##*.}"
    ext="$(printf '%s' "$ext" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"  # bash 3.2-safe lowercasing
    case "$ext" in
        docx)        render_docx "$f" ;;
        xlsx)        render_xlsx "$f" ;;
        pptx)        render_pptx "$f" ;;
        doc|odt|rtf) render_legacy "$f" docx ;;
        xls|ods)     render_legacy "$f" xlsx ;;
        ppt|odp)     render_legacy "$f" pptx ;;
        *)
            err "unsupported file type: .$ext"
            err "supported: docx xlsx pptx doc xls ppt odt ods odp rtf"
            exit 2
            ;;
    esac
}

main() {
    local file=""
    while (($#)); do
        case "$1" in
            -p|--preview) PREVIEW=1; shift ;;
            -w|--width)
                [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { err "--width requires a value"; exit 2; }
                WIDTH="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --width=*) WIDTH="${1#*=}"; shift ;;
            -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
            --) shift; while (($#)); do file="$1"; shift; done; break ;;
            -*) err "unknown option: $1"; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
            *)
                if [[ -z "$file" ]]; then file="$1"; else err "too many files: $1"; exit 2; fi
                shift ;;
        esac
    done

    if [[ -z "$file" ]]; then
        err "expected a FILE"
        usage >&2
        exit 2
    fi
    if [[ ! -r "$file" ]]; then
        err "file not readable: $file"
        exit 1
    fi
    render "$file"
}

main "$@"

```

1	#!/bin/bash
2	# Restore globally-installed agent skills from ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json.
3	#
4	# The skills CLI (vercel-labs/skills) does not yet support `npx skills install -g`
5	# from a lock file (issues #283 / #549), so we hand-roll restore here:
6	#   1. The lock file itself is chezmoi-managed via dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl
7	#      (merger that preserves per-machine state).
8	#   2. This script reads the merged lock and, for any entry whose
9	#      ~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md is missing, runs
10	#      `npx skills add <source> -s <name> -g -y` to (re)install it.
11	#
12	# Trigger: changes to the merger script's $managed block (the source-of-truth list).
13	#   merger: {{ include "dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl" | sha256sum }}
14	#
15	# Idempotent: a re-run with no missing skills is a no-op.
16	# See: docs/tools/agent-skills.md
17	
18	set -eu
19	export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.npm-global/bin:$PATH"
20	
21	info()    { printf '\033[0;34m[INFO]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
22	warn()    { printf '\033[1;33m[WARN]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
23	success() { printf '\033[0;32m[SUCCESS]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
24	
25	LOCK="$HOME/.agents/.skill-lock.json"
26	
27	if [ ! -f "$LOCK" ]; then
28	  warn "Global lock file not found at $LOCK — skipping (chezmoi apply should create it)."
29	  exit 0
30	fi
31	
32	if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
33	  warn "jq not installed; cannot parse $LOCK — skipping. Run \`chezmoi apply\` again after the base ansible role finishes."
34	  exit 0
35	fi
36	
37	if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
38	  warn "npx not installed; cannot restore global skills — skipping."
39	  exit 0
40	fi
41	
42	# Collect names of skills declared in the lock that are missing on disk.
43	missing=()
44	while IFS=$'\t' read -r name source; do
45	  [ -z "$name" ] && continue
46	  if [ ! -f "$HOME/.agents/skills/$name/SKILL.md" ]; then
47	    missing+=("$name"$'\t'"$source")
48	  fi
49	done < <(jq -r '.skills | to_entries[] | "\(.key)\t\(.value.source)"' "$LOCK")
50	
51	if [ ${#missing[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
52	  info "All globally-managed agent skills present; nothing to install."
53	  exit 0
54	fi
55	
56	info "Restoring ${#missing[@]} missing global skill(s) via \`npx skills add ... -g\`"
57	for entry in "${missing[@]}"; do
58	  name="${entry%%$'\t'*}"
59	  source="${entry##*$'\t'}"
60	  info "  → $name (from $source)"
61	  # Note: -s <name> filters to one skill within multi-skill repos.
62	  # No -a flag → npx prompts auto-detect agents from $HOME/.<agent>/ presence.
63	  if npx -y skills@latest add "$source" -s "$name" -g -y >/dev/null 2>&1; then
64	    success "    installed $name"
65	  else
66	    warn "    failed to install $name (continuing)"
67	  fi
68	done
69	
70	success "Global agent skills sync complete."
71
```
</details></tool-use>

# yazi plugin lockfile — managed by chezmoi (source: dot_config/yazi/package.toml).
#
# Materialized into ~/.config/yazi/plugins/ by `ya pkg install`, run automatically
# on every `chezmoi apply` via
# .chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_45_yazi_plugins.sh.tmpl (hash-gated on
# this file). `ya pkg install` READS but never rewrites this file, so there is no
# chezmoi drift.
#
# Add a plugin:    `ya pkg add <owner>/<repo>:<plugin>` then copy the regenerated
#                  ~/.config/yazi/package.toml back here (`chezmoi re-add` / cp).
# Upgrade plugins: `ya pkg upgrade` (see scripts/upgrade_tools.sh /
#                  `just upgrade-yazi-plugins`) then copy back — install-only by
#                  design, apply never bumps revs.
#
# piper.yazi: generic "pipe any shell command as a previewer" plugin. Used by the
# Office previewers in yazi.toml (`piper -- view-office --preview ...`).
# See docs/tools/office-viewers.md.
[[plugin.deps]]
use = "yazi-rs/plugins:piper"
rev = "8577ec8"
hash = "e0d59bd47866a6a574c74574097e5070"

[flavor]
deps = []

```tmpl
#!/bin/bash
# Install yazi plugins declared in the managed lockfile via `ya pkg install`.
# Materializes ~/.config/yazi/plugins/ (piper.yazi, …) so the Office previewers
# in yazi.toml work. `ya pkg install` reads but never rewrites package.toml, so
# there is no chezmoi drift.
#
# Re-runs only when the lockfile changes:
#   package.toml: {{ include "dot_config/yazi/package.toml" | sha256sum }}
#
# Install-only by design — upgrades are `ya pkg upgrade`
# (`just upgrade-yazi-plugins`). See docs/tools/office-viewers.md.

set -eu
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

{{ if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}
if [[ -f /opt/homebrew/bin/brew ]]; then
    eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
elif [[ -f /usr/local/bin/brew ]]; then
    eval "$(/usr/local/bin/brew shellenv)"
fi
{{ else -}}
if [[ -d /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew ]]; then
    eval "$(/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
elif [[ -d "$HOME/.linuxbrew" ]]; then
    eval "$("$HOME/.linuxbrew/bin/brew" shellenv)"
fi
{{ end -}}

info()    { printf '\033[0;34m[INFO]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
warn()    { printf '\033[1;33m[WARN]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
success() { printf '\033[0;32m[SUCCESS]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }

# `ya` is yazi's CLI companion (ships with yazi). `ya pkg` replaced the older
# `ya pack`. Skip gracefully on fresh boxes where the devtools role hasn't
# installed yazi yet (this run-script is 45, ansible roles run at 20).
if ! command -v ya >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    info "ya (yazi CLI) not found; skipping yazi plugin install (devtools role installs yazi)"
    exit 0
fi
if ! command -v yazi >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    info "yazi not found; skipping yazi plugin install"
    exit 0
fi
if [ ! -f "$HOME/.config/yazi/package.toml" ]; then
    warn "yazi package.toml not found; skipping (chezmoi apply should deploy it)"
    exit 0
fi

10	|---------|-----------|----------------|----------|
11	| `readurl <url>` | [Jina AI Reader](https://jina.ai/reader) (`r.jina.ai`) | remote | Default. Any page, zero local deps beyond `glow`. Fast. |
12	| `readlocal <url>` | [trafilatura](https://trafilatura.readthedocs.io/) | local (Python) | Privacy-sensitive or offline. Well-tuned for news/blog articles. |
13	| `readnode <url>` | [readability-cli](https://gitlab.com/gardenappl/readability-cli) (Mozilla Readability port) | local (Node) | Same algorithm as Firefox/Safari Reader View. Often the best article fidelity. |
14	| `readraw <url>` | `curl \| pandoc -f html -t gfm` | local | Escape hatch: docs / reference pages where article extraction strips too much. |
15	
16	All four pipe into [`glow`](https://github.com/charmbracelet/glow) for rendering and paging, and all four wrap the fetch in `try_direct_then_proxy` so pages reachable without a proxy pay zero overhead.
17	
18	Source: `dot_config/zsh/tools/55_web_reader.zsh` (readers) and `dot_config/zsh/tools/50_networking.zsh` (proxy helpers).
19	
20	## The landscape — why four tools, not one
21	
22	"Read a webpage as markdown" decomposes into three independent choices:
23	
24	1. **Fetch** — `curl`, headless browser (for JS-heavy pages), or a remote service that fetches on your behalf.
25	2. **Extract** — strip navigation, ads, comments, footers; keep the article. Or don't, if you want the whole page.
26	3. **Render** — markdown into the terminal; `glow`, `mdcat`, or plain stdout.
27	
28	No single tool owns the full pipeline well:
29	
30	- [**Jina AI Reader**](https://jina.ai/reader) collapses fetch + extract into a single HTTP GET: `https://r.jina.ai/<url>` returns ready-to-read markdown. Zero install. Trade-offs: remote service (privacy / availability), and may itself be blocked from some networks — fall back through a proxy in that case.
```
</details></tool-use>

```md
# View Office Documents in the Terminal

Open and preview Microsoft Office (`.docx` / `.xlsx` / `.pptx`), legacy binary (`.doc` / `.xls` / `.ppt`), and OpenDocument (`.odt` / `.ods` / `.odp`) files without leaving the terminal — no Microsoft Office, no GUI.

There is no single tool that views everything well, so this repo wires a small **per-format + two-mode** stack behind one dispatcher, [`view-office`](#the-view-office-dispatcher), and hooks it into the [yazi](tmux/README.md) file manager for inline previews.

## TL;DR

| Format | Interactive (TUI / pager) | Quick preview (stdout) |
|---|---|---|
| Word `.docx` | [`doxx`](https://github.com/bgreenwell/doxx) | `doxx --export ansi` |
| Excel `.xlsx` | [`visidata`](https://www.visidata.org/) (`vd`) | `markitdown \| glow` |
| PowerPoint `.pptx` | `markitdown \| glow` (pager) | `markitdown \| glow` |
| Legacy `.doc/.xls/.ppt`, OpenDocument `.odt/.ods/.odp`, `.rtf` | LibreOffice → OOXML twin → above | same, converted first |

\```console
$ view-office report.docx                 # interactive: rich TUI (doxx)
$ view-office --preview budget.xlsx        # markdown/ANSI to stdout
$ view-office legacy-memo.doc              # LibreOffice converts, then doxx
\```

## The `view-office` dispatcher

`view-office` (source: `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_view-office`, deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin/`, on `PATH`) is a small bash script that dispatches by file extension:

\```text
view-office [--preview] [--width N] FILE
  -p, --preview    render to stdout (ANSI/markdown) instead of launching a TUI
  -w, --width N    wrap width for --preview (default: $COLUMNS or 100)
  -h, --help       show help
\```

Two modes:

- **Interactive** (default) — launches the best full-screen viewer for the type: `doxx` for Word, `visidata` for Excel, a `glow` pager for PowerPoint.
- **Preview** (`--preview`) — emits ANSI/markdown to stdout. This is the single source of truth that the [yazi previewer](#yazi-inline-previews) (and any future `tv` / `fzf` integration) calls, so preview logic lives in exactly one place.

Legacy binary and OpenDocument formats are converted to their modern OOXML twin with **LibreOffice headless** into a temp dir, then re-dispatched to the handler above (e.g. `.doc → .docx → doxx`). Missing tools produce an actionable install hint and exit 2 — nothing fails silently.

> **Why bash, not the `uv run --script` pattern** used by `pqsum`/`yth`/`mlf`? `view-office` sits on yazi's preview hot-path (invoked on every file hover). uv/Python startup (~100–200 ms) would make previews feel laggy; bash dispatch is ~5 ms.

## The tools

### doxx — terminal-native Word viewer

[doxx](https://github.com/bgreenwell/doxx) renders `.docx` directly in the terminal: bold/italic/headings, smart tables, LaTeX equations, and inline images (Kitty/iTerm2/Sixel). It also exports non-interactively — `doxx FILE --export ansi|markdown|text|csv|json` — which is what `view-office --preview` uses for Word.

- **macOS:** `brew install doxx` (it's in **homebrew-core** — the README's `bgreenwell/tap/doxx` is stale; that tap ships `xleak`/`lstr`, not doxx).
- **Linux:** GitHub release `.tar.xz` (cargo-dist, static musl on x86_64) → `~/.local/bin/doxx`, installed by the `devtools` ansible role.

### visidata — spreadsheet multitool

Already in the repo (see [Data Viewers](../shells/aliases.md#data-viewers)). `vd file.xlsx` opens a fast, vim-keyed TUI over the sheet. Used for **interactive** Excel; for previews, `markitdown` renders the sheet to a markdown table instead (visidata is TUI-only).

### markitdown — Office → Markdown

[Microsoft MarkItDown](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown) converts `.docx/.xlsx/.pptx` (and more) to Markdown, optimized for LLM/RAG pipelines. It is the universal preview engine for Excel and PowerPoint here, because **pandoc cannot read `.pptx` or `.xlsx`** (pandoc only *writes* pptx; it reads docx/odt/epub but not the spreadsheet/presentation formats). Installed as a uv tool (`python_uv_tools`).

> **Gotcha:** the bare `markitdown` package ships **no format converters** — they live in optional extras. This repo installs `markitdown[docx,xlsx,pptx]`; without the extras every Office file raises `MissingDependencyException`. (Not `[all]` — that adds pdf/audio/youtube/azure bloat.)

### LibreOffice — legacy-format fallback

Only `soffice --headless --convert-to` can read the old binary formats (`.doc/.xls/.ppt`) and OpenDocument. Heavy (~hundreds of MB), so it's a **fallback**, installed by `devtools` (macOS cask / `libreoffice-writer,calc,impress` on Debian with recommends off). On macOS `soffice` is not on `PATH`; `view-office` resolves the `.app` bundle path itself. No-root Linux installs skip it and `view-office` prints an install hint for legacy files.

## Yazi inline previews

Hovering an Office file in [yazi](tmux/README.md) renders a preview in the right pane. This is the repo's first yazi **plugin** integration, via the [`ya pkg`](#the-ya-pkg-plugin-mechanism) manager and the [`piper.yazi`](https://github.com/yazi-rs/plugins/tree/main/piper.yazi) plugin ("pipe any shell command as a previewer"):

\```toml
# dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml
[plugin]
prepend_previewers = [
  { url = "*.docx", run = 'piper -- view-office --preview --width "$w" "$1"' },
  # … .xlsx .pptx .doc .xls .ppt .odt .ods .odp .rtf
]
\```

`piper.yazi` passes `$w` (preview width) and `$1` (file path); the command's stdout becomes the preview. The `run` string and `view-office`'s `--preview`/`--width` interface are a **contract** — change one, change the other.

### The `ya pkg` plugin mechanism

`ya pkg` is Yazi's plugin manager (`ya` is the CLI companion shipped with yazi). It clones a plugin, copies it into `~/.config/yazi/plugins/`, and locks its version in `~/.config/yazi/package.toml`.

In this repo the lockfile is **chezmoi-managed** (`dot_config/yazi/package.toml`) and the plugins are materialized by a hash-gated run-script:

| Piece | Path | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Lockfile (SSOT) | `dot_config/yazi/package.toml` | pins `yazi-rs/plugins:piper` (rev + hash) |
| Installer | `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_45_yazi_plugins.sh.tmpl` | runs `ya pkg install` when the lockfile changes |
| Previewer wiring | `dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml` `[plugin]` | maps Office extensions → `piper -- view-office …` |

`ya pkg install` **reads but never rewrites** `package.toml`, so there's no chezmoi drift. It is install-only by design (like the rest of the repo) — bump plugin versions with `ya pkg upgrade` (`just upgrade-yazi-plugins`), then copy the regenerated `~/.config/yazi/package.toml` back into the source.

Add another yazi plugin:

\```bash
ya pkg add <owner>/<repo>:<plugin>       # installs + updates ~/.config/yazi/package.toml
cp ~/.config/yazi/package.toml "$(chezmoi source-path ~/.config/yazi/package.toml)"
\```

## Where things live

| Surface | Path |
|---|---|
| Dispatcher CLI | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_view-office` |
| Completions (zsh/bash) | `dot_config/{zsh/tools,bash}/55_view_office_completion.*` |
| doxx / LibreOffice install | `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` |
| markitdown install | `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml` |
| yazi previewers | `dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml` |
| yazi plugin lockfile + installer | `dot_config/yazi/package.toml`, `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_45_yazi_plugins.sh.tmpl` |
| Upgrades | `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh` (`just upgrade-yazi-plugins`) |

## Gotchas

- **`markitdown` needs extras** — see the box above. `markitdown[docx,xlsx,pptx]`, not bare `markitdown`.
- **pandoc ≠ Office reader** — it cannot read `.pptx`/`.xlsx`. Use `markitdown` for those. (pandoc still powers the [web reader](web-reader.md) for HTML.)
- **Uppercase extensions** — the yazi `url` globs are lowercase (`*.docx`); a file named `Report.DOCX` won't trigger the previewer (running `view-office` directly still works — it lowercases internally).
- **LibreOffice cold start** — the first legacy-format conversion spins up a headless soffice profile (~1–2 s); previews of `.doc/.xls/.ppt` are slower than modern formats.
- **PATH in yazi previews** — `piper` runs the command via `sh`; `view-office` must be on the `PATH` yazi inherited. Launch yazi from a configured shell so `~/.dotfiles/bin` is present.

## See also

- [Data Viewers](../shells/aliases.md#data-viewers) — VisiData wrappers.
- [Web reader](web-reader.md) — read HTML pages as markdown (the pandoc/`glow` sibling).
- [tool-managers.md](../this_repo/tool-managers.md) — install-side index (doxx, markitdown, libreoffice, `ya pkg`).

```text
43	## Category matrix
44	
45	| Category | What actually happens |
46	| --- | --- |
47	| `externals` | `chezmoi upgrade` (the chezmoi binary itself) + `chezmoi apply --refresh-externals` (force-refresh the 168h externals: oh-my-zsh, TPM, toolkami.rb, fzf). First because a chezmoi version bump may change how later steps behave. |
48	| `brew` | `brew update` → `brew upgrade` → `brew upgrade --cask --greedy` → `brew bundle --file=~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile` *without* `--no-upgrade` → `Brewfile.{darwin,linux}` → `brew cleanup`. macOS pre-warms the shared sudo session via [`scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh`](../../scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh) so cask pkg installers that shell out to `sudo /usr/sbin/installer` find a live ticket. |
49	| `mise` | `mise self-update --yes` + `mise upgrade` (honours the version constraints in `~/.config/mise/config.toml`). `self-update` warns, rather than fails, when mise was installed via brew/apt. |
50	| `uv` | Detects install style by binary path (Homebrew vs curl-installer) and dispatches to the right channel: `brew upgrade uv` for Homebrew/Linuxbrew installs, `uv self update` for the standalone curl installer. Then `uv tool upgrade --all`. Covers every tool listed in [`python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml`](../../dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml) and [`llm_tools/defaults/main.yml`](../../dot_ansible/roles/llm_tools/defaults/main.yml). The `python_uv_tools` ansible role does the same dispatch automatically when uv is below `min_uv_version` — see [`docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md`](uv-bootstrap.md). |
51	| `npm` | `npm -g update`, falling back to `mise exec -- npm -g update` when `npm` is not directly on PATH (same detection as [`js_cli_tools`](../../dot_ansible/roles/js_cli_tools/tasks/main.yml) / [`bitwarden`](../../dot_ansible/roles/bitwarden/tasks/main.yml)). |
52	| `cargo` | If absent, bootstraps the `cargo-update` crate, then `cargo install-update -a`. Covers pueue (Linux) plus any future entries in [`rust_cargo_tools/defaults/main.yml`](../../dot_ansible/roles/rust_cargo_tools/defaults/main.yml). |
53	| `go` | Parses tool names from [`go_tools/defaults/main.yml`](../../dot_ansible/roles/go_tools/defaults/main.yml) and runs `go install <pkg>@latest` per entry (strips the pinned version), installing into `~/.local/bin` via `GOBIN`. Resolves go via the mise shim; `SKIPPED` when Go is absent (`installExtraRuntimes=false`). |
54	| `dotnet` | Parses tool names from [`dotnet_tools/defaults/main.yml`](../../dot_ansible/roles/dotnet_tools/defaults/main.yml) and runs `dotnet tool update --global <name>` per tool (via the mise dotnet shim). Falls back to `dotnet tool list --global` if parsing finds nothing. |
55	| `gem` | `gem update --system` + `gem update` via the mise ruby shim. |
56	| `flatpak` | `flatpak update --user --noninteractive --assumeyes` for user-scope Flathub apps (Discord et al. when `discordChannel=flatpak` — see [`docs/playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md`](../playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md)). Skipped when `flatpak` is absent OR when no user-scope apps are installed. System-scope (`flatpak update --system`) is intentionally NOT covered — it requires `sudo` and is rare in this repo's flow; run manually if needed. |
57	| `warp` | **Linux only.** `sudo apt-get update` + `sudo apt-get install --only-upgrade -y warp-terminal` via the shared sudo session. macOS Warp is handled by `cat_brew` (cask `warp` + `--greedy`); this category short-circuits with `SKIPPED` on Darwin. The on-disk binary is replaced but the running Warp process is **not** restarted — quit + relaunch Warp to load the new version. The in-app `warp_finish_update <token>` graceful-restart only works from inside a live Warp session (Warp-injected shell function, not on `$PATH` otherwise) — see [`docs/tools/warp.md`](../tools/warp.md) for the full mechanism. |
58	| `agents` | Re-runs the official `curl \| bash` installers for **tools already present** only — Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor CLI, Ollama (Linux), llmfit (Linux), RTK. Bootstrap list mirrors [`coding_agents`](../../dot_ansible/roles/coding_agents/tasks/main.yml). |
59	| `atuin` | macOS: `brew upgrade atuin` (no-op when atuin was installed via the upstream installer rather than brew). Linux: re-runs `curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://setup.atuin.sh \| env ATUIN_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1 sh` so the upstream installer drops the new binary into `~/.atuin/bin/` while leaving PATH wiring to [`dot_config/shell/15_atuin.sh`](../../dot_config/shell/15_atuin.sh). Skipped with `SKIPPED` if `atuin` is not on PATH. The local SQLite history (`~/.local/share/atuin/`) and config (`~/.config/atuin/config.toml`) are untouched. |
60	| `plugins` | `nvim --headless "+Lazy! sync" +qa` → `~/.tmux/plugins/tpm/bin/update_plugins all` → refresh installed `claude-hud` via [`claude_hud_sync.py`](../../dot_ansible/roles/coding_agents/files/claude_hud_sync.py) → `pre-commit autoupdate` (on the dotfiles repo root) → `tldr --update` → `gh extension upgrade --all`. Each step is guarded on the relevant binary being present. |
61	
62	### Run order
63	
64	```mermaid
65	flowchart LR
66	    externals["externals<br/>(chezmoi + externals)"] --> brew
67	    brew["brew<br/>(formulas + casks greedy + Brewfile)"] --> mise
68	    mise["mise<br/>(self-update + runtimes)"] --> uv
69	    uv["uv<br/>(self update + tools)"] --> npm
70	    npm["npm<br/>(-g update)"] --> cargo
71	    cargo["cargo<br/>(install-update -a)"] --> go
72	    go["go<br/>(install @latest)"] --> dotnet
73	    dotnet["dotnet<br/>(tool update --global)"] --> gem
74	    gem["gem<br/>(gem update)"] --> flatpak
75	    flatpak["flatpak<br/>(--user update)"] --> warp
76	    warp["warp<br/>(Linux apt-only)"] --> atuin
77	    atuin["atuin<br/>(brew or setup.atuin.sh)"] --> agents
78	    agents["agents<br/>(curl \| bash installers)"] --> plugins
79	    plugins["plugins<br/>(Lazy, TPM, pre-commit, tldr, gh)"] --> summary((Summary))
80	```
81	
82	Rationale: package managers themselves go first (`externals` to maybe swap chezmoi; `brew` because mise/uv/npm/cargo/dotnet/gem may be Homebrew-installed; `mise` before the language-scoped ones because `mise upgrade` can swap the runtime `npm`/`cargo`/`go`/`dotnet`/`gem` belong to). `agents` + `plugins` last because they depend on everything above being current.
83	
84	`claude-hud` stays out of [`.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl`](../../.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl): it uses a versioned cache path and rewrites `~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json`, so it fits the explicit `plugins` upgrade path better than chezmoi externals. Upstream `v0.0.12+` also switched usage rendering to Claude Code's official stdin `rate_limits`, which means the old credential-derived `Max` badge may disappear after upgrade.
85	
86	## Semantics: best-effort, not all-or-nothing
87
```
</details></tool-use>

Done. Terminal Office-document viewing is fully implemented, wired, documented, and verified end-to-end.

## What shipped

**Tooling**
- **doxx** (Word TUI) → `devtools` role: macOS `brew install doxx` (it's in **homebrew-core** — the README's `bgreenwell/tap/doxx` is stale), Linux via cargo-dist `.tar.xz` (worktrunk-style block, static-musl on x86_64).
- **markitdown** (Office→MD) → `python_uv_tools` as `markitdown[docx,xlsx,pptx]` + `needs_modern_gcc`.
- **LibreOffice** (legacy `.doc/.xls/.ppt` fallback) → `devtools`: macOS cask, Debian `libreoffice-writer/calc/impress` (no-recommends).

**Integration**
- `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_view-office` — bash dispatcher (bash, not uv, for yazi preview latency): per-extension routing, `--preview` mode, legacy→OOXML conversion via soffice, actionable missing-tool hints.
- yazi previewers via the repo's **first `ya pkg` plugin mechanism**: managed `dot_config/yazi/package.toml` + hash-gated `run_onchange_after_45_yazi_plugins.sh.tmpl` (`ya pkg install`) + 10 `piper --  view-office --preview` entries in `yazi.toml`.
- Strategy-B completions (NN=55) for both shells.

**Docs/upgrades** — new `docs/tools/office-viewers.md` (+mkdocs nav/i18n), tool-managers.md (3 A–Z rows + piper + new § 15 `ya pkg` mechanism + decision-tree branch), README, SKILL.md, zsh-completions §F, a CLAUDE.md cross-file row, and a `yazi-plugins` upgrade category (`just upgrade-yazi-plugins`).

## Bugs caught during verification (would have silently shipped)
1. **markitdown reads zero Office files without extras** — bare package throws `MissingDependencyException`; fixed to `[docx,xlsx,pptx]` (verified xlsx/pptx now render).
2. **doxx isn't in `bgreenwell/tap`** (only `xleak`/`lstr`) — it's in homebrew-core; and its Linux assets are `.tar.xz` target-triples, not the README's `.tar.gz`.
3. **Drive-by:** `upgrade_tools.sh`'s arg allowlist was missing `go` too (so `just upgrade-go` was broken) — fixed alongside `yazi-plugins`.

## Verified
docx/xlsx/pptx `--preview` render with real tools; edge/error paths; ansible `--syntax-check` (both playbooks); TOML/YAML validity; `ya pkg install` idempotency (never rewrites the lockfile → no drift); scoped `chezmoi apply` → `view-office` on PATH + functional; upgrade dry-run dispatch; mkdocs builds the page warning-free; all pre-commit hooks pass.

**Not headless-testable (manual):** live yazi hover-preview (needs a TTY) and legacy-format conversion (needs LibreOffice, not installed locally — the degradation path was verified). Full-machine `chezmoi apply` will install doxx/markitdown/LibreOffice via ansible and fire the `ya pkg install` run-script; I did a *scoped* apply to avoid triggering the LibreOffice cask download here.
